Question: According to KOC.SA.002, how often must an in-service scaffold be re-inspected by an authorized Scaffolding Inspector, whether or not it has been used?
D: Only after alterations or bad weather
Reference: Cl. 4.1.3 / 5.1.6: inspection before first use, after alteration, after adverse weather and every 7 days thereafter.

Question: Above what wind speed does KOC.SA.002 prohibit work on or from scaffolds?
Reference: Cl. 5.1.3 c): work on scaffolds is prohibited during storms or high winds (wind speed more than 65 km/h).

Question: An elevated scaffold work area requires at least two means of exit when the horizontal travel distance to the nearest exit ladder exceeds:
Reference: Cl. 5.1.3 f): where horizontal travel distance to the nearest exit exceeds 15 m (50 ft), at least two means of exit are required.

Question: A worker is setting up a portable ladder against a structure. Which set-up ratio meets the KOC.SA.002 requirement of approximately 76 degrees?
A: 1 m out for every 2 m up
B: 1 m out for every 3 m up
C: 1 m out for every 4 m up
D: 1 m out for every 6 m up
Reference: Cl. 5.2.2 h): ladders shall be set at an angle of 76 degrees (1 m out for 4 m up).

Question: Where no adequate handhold is provided at the landing, a portable ladder must extend above the landing place by at least:
Reference: Cl. 5.2.2 i): the ladder must rise at least 1.05 m (3.5 ft) above the landing place.

Question: Without a supporting risk assessment, what is the minimum distance a scaffold may be erected from an existing excavation?
Reference: Cl. 5.1.3 aa): no scaffold shall be erected less than 3 m from an existing excavation; a shorter distance only based on a risk assessment.

Question: What minimum experience does KOC.SA.002 require for a Scaffolding Supervisor, in addition to certified erection and dismantling training?
A: 3 years in scaffolding, with no supervisory requirement
B: 5 years in scaffolding, including at least 1 year as a supervisor
C: 5 years in scaffolding, including at least 3 years as a supervisor
D: 10 years in scaffolding, including at least 2 years as a supervisor
Reference: Cl. 5.1.2 b): minimum 5 years' experience in scaffolding jobs, of which at least one year in a supervisory role.

Question: What is the maximum permitted height of a portable stepladder under KOC.SA.002?
Reference: Cl. 5.2.3 f): portable stepladders shall not exceed 20 ft (6.1 m) in height.

Question: A scaffold has been inspected and certified safe for use. What colour Scaffolding Tag should be displayed at its access points?
Reference: Cl. 4.1.5 / 5.1.6: scaffolds certified safe for use carry a Green Scaffolding Tag; incomplete or unsafe scaffolds carry a Red tag.

Question: A worker finds that the Scaffolding Tag holder at a scaffold access point is empty. What does this mean?
A: The scaffold shall not be used
B: The scaffold is due for its 7-day inspection
C: The tag is being re-printed and work may continue
D: The scaffold is safe for light duty only
Reference: Cl. 2.0 / 5.1.6: an empty Scaffolding Tag holder denotes that the scaffold shall not be used.

Question: In addition to the required diploma or science degree, what minimum scaffolding experience must a Scaffold Inspector have?
Reference: Cl. 5.1.2 a): Scaffold Inspector — diploma (Engineering) or science graduate with five (5) years' experience in scaffold erection, modification and disassembly.

Question: What minimum experience is required for a Scaffolder, in addition to certified erection and dismantling training?
Reference: Cl. 5.1.2 c): Scaffolders shall have certified training and three (3) years' experience in the related field.

Question: How should scaffold components be brought down from height during dismantling?
A: Dropped onto a heap of sand below
B: Thrown into a barricaded drop zone
C: Slid down a ladder used as a chute
D: Lowered hand to hand or by gin wheel
Reference: Cl. 5.1.1 c): scaffold materials shall not be thrown or dropped; they shall be raised or lowered hand to hand or by crane, gin wheel or other suitable means.

Question: What certification does KOC.SA.002 require for a gin wheel used on site to raise scaffold materials?
A: No certification if load is under 50 kg
B: Visual check by the Scaffolder only
Reference: Cl. 5.1.1 c): gin wheel used at site shall be third party certified; the worksite supervisor ensures wheel and rope are in good condition.

Question: Which of the following shall NOT be used as a means of access to a scaffold platform?
Reference: Cl. 5.1.3 g): portable or attached ladders, stair towers, ramps etc. shall be used; cross braces shall not be used as a means of access.

Question: When must scaffold ties be fixed during erection?
B: Only when the scaffold is complete
Reference: Cl. 5.1.3 l): ties shall be fixed as erection proceeds, not when the scaffold is complete.

Question: How many scaffold erection, modification or dismantling jobs may one Scaffolding Supervisor supervise at the same time?
A: As many as are on the same site
Reference: Cl. 5.1.3 z): a Scaffolding Supervisor can supervise only one scaffold erection, modification or dismantling job at any given time.

Question: Materials must not be stored on or under a scaffold. At what minimum distance from the scaffold area should they be stored?
Reference: Cl. 5.1.6: no materials shall be stored over or under the scaffold; materials shall be stored 3 m away from the scaffold erected area.

Question: Rejected scaffold materials must be removed from project sites within how many working days?
Reference: Cl. 4.1.7: Controlling Team shall ensure all rejected materials are removed from project sites within fifteen (15) working days.

Question: How many persons may be on a portable ladder at any one time?
Reference: Cl. 5.2.2 s): only one person shall be on the ladder at any one time.

Question: When working from a portable ladder, the working position shall be no higher than how many rungs from the top?
Reference: Cl. 5.2.2 t): the working position shall not be less than five rungs from the top of the ladder.

Question: What is the maximum validity of a Hot, Cold or Radiography Work Permit from its date of issue, subject to renewal by the Permit Issuer?
Reference: Cl. 5.4: Hot / Cold / Radiography permits are valid for a maximum of seven consecutive days from the date of issue, subject to renewal.

Question: A Work Permit endorsement or renewal remains valid for a maximum of:
Reference: Cl. 5.8 e): each endorsement / renewal is valid for a maximum of one shift (12 hours) or as recorded by the Permit Issuer.

Question: A worksite was gas tested and certified gas free at 07:00, but the job could not start until 09:30. What must happen before work starts?
A: Work may start because the certificate is valid for the shift
B: Work may start if the Worksite Supervisor signs the permit
C: A new gas test must be carried out
D: Work may start if a fire watch is posted
Reference: Cl. 5.15 b): if work has not started within 2 hours of a gas test, the gas free certification becomes invalid and a new test is required.

Question: What is the maximum flammable gas reading permitted for authorizing Hot Work under the KOC Permit to Work Procedure?
Reference: Cl. 5.13.2 / 5.15 g): the maximum LEL permissible for authorized Hot Work is 0% LEL.

Question: During cold work on a flowline, 0% LEL cannot be achieved despite depressurizing, venting and purging. Under what condition may the work proceed?
A: Below 10% LEL, continuously monitored, with an approved Method Statement
B: Below 20% LEL, with all workers wearing breathing apparatus sets
C: Below 25% LEL, with a fire watch and extinguishers posted at site
D: Any LEL reading, with verbal approval from the Permit Issuer
Reference: Cl. 5.13.1 c): work may be carried out ensuring LEL does not exceed 10% under continuous monitoring; a reviewed and approved Method Statement is mandatory.

Question: What is the maximum period a Work Permit can remain suspended before it must be cancelled and signed off?
A: 24 hours, after which it is cancelled
B: 3 days, after which it is cancelled
C: 5 days, or permit expiry if sooner
Reference: Cl. 5.11: a Work Permit can be suspended for a maximum of 5 days or until expiry of its validity, whichever is sooner.

Question: What is the minimum fire extinguisher provision for each Hot Work location under KOC.SA.004?
Reference: Cl. 5.16 a): a minimum of two fire extinguishers (9 kg Monnex or 12 kg DCP) within 7.5 m of each hot work location.

Question: Unless otherwise stated in the permit, how long is an Excavation Notification valid from the date the Asset Owner signs it?
Reference: Cl. 5.13.6 e): the Excavation Notification is valid for 90 days from the date of issuance.

Question: What is the minimum passing score for the PTW qualifying written test for Permit Issuers, Permit Applicants and Worksite Supervisors?
Reference: Cl. 5.7 b): the passing score for the PTW qualifying test shall be a minimum of 70%.

Question: Under KOC.SA.004, mechanical excavation is NOT allowed within what radius of any underground facility?
Reference: Cl. 5.13.6 a): mechanical excavation is not allowed inside the plant or facility or within 5 m radius of any underground facilities.

Question: Under the KOC Permit to Work system, which of the following is a CERTIFICATE rather than a work permit?
Reference: Cl. 5.3: the PTW system has four types of Work Permits (Cold, Hot, Radiography, Vehicle/Mobile Equipment Entry) and one Certificate (Confined Space Entry).

Question: Who authorizes (issues) a Work Permit for work in an operating area?
A: Permit Issuer of the Asset Operating Team
B: Safety Officer of the Asset HSE Team
C: Permit Applicant of the Controlling Team
Reference: Cl. 2.0 / 4.2: the Permit Issuer represents the Asset Operating Team in whose area of control the work is carried out.

Question: How long is a Vehicle Entry Permit valid for a vehicle entering a hazardous area?
Reference: Cl. 5.4 / 5.13.5: Vehicle Entry Permit valid for one continuous shift; Mobile Equipment Entry valid up to 7 consecutive days.

Question: Which of the following activities is listed as Critical Work in KOC.SA.004?
B: Working at a height of 1.5 metres
C: Heavy lifting of more than 50 tons
D: Cold work on a 220 V lighting circuit
Reference: Cl. 2.0 Critical Work examples: work at height > 1.8 m, excavation > 1.2 m, HV > 440 V, heavy lifting > 50 tons, etc.

Question: How often must the PTW Authorization Card be revalidated after refresher training?
A: Every 2 years, or contract period if earlier
B: Every 3 years, or on change of job
C: Every year, regardless of contract period
D: Every 5 years, at the HSE Induction Center
Reference: Cl. 5.7 e): revalidated on expiry — every 2 years or contract period, whichever is earlier — after refresher training.

Question: A contractor's Worksite Supervisor fails the PTW qualifying test. When may he re-appear for the test?
A: The next day, without any approval needed
B: After 1 month, with HSE Group approval
C: After 1 week, with Controlling Team approval
D: After 6 months, with Asset Owner approval
Reference: Cl. 5.7 f): he can re-appear after 1 week from the date of the last test with approval of the Controlling Team.

Question: A mistake is made while filling a manual Work Permit. How must it be corrected?
A: Page torn out and a fresh copy started by the PI
B: Single line through it, initialled by PA and PI
C: Wrong entry overwritten neatly in ink by the PA
D: Correction fluid applied, then the entry rewritten
Reference: Cl. 5.8 b): mistakes crossed out with a single line and initialled by PA and PI; overwriting or correction fluid invalidates the permit.

Question: In an emergency with actual or potential loss of life, how may urgent safety work begin without a Work Permit?
A: Verbal OK from PI or senior KOC person, logged
B: Not possible without a written permit
C: Verbal OK from any contractor supervisor
D: Only after a printed e-WP is issued
Reference: Cl. 5.1 d): PI or senior-most KOC personnel may verbally allow the work; recorded in the Operation Logbook and signed by the PI; permit prepared as soon as practical.

Question: Before radiography starts, when are the Public Address (PA) announcements made?
A: Only at the moment radiography starts
Reference: Cl. 5.13.3 f): PA announcement 30 minutes prior and a further announcement 5 minutes prior to radiography commencement.

Question: For Hot Work in a hazardous area, what minimum reach must the pressurized 2½-inch fire water hose have?
Reference: Cl. 5.16 b): a 2½" pressurized water hose capable of reaching a minimum distance of 30 m from the hot work location.

Question: How many Fire Team-approved fire extinguishers must mobile equipment such as a welding machine have to enter a hazardous area?
Reference: Cl. 5.13.5 b): mobile equipment must have at least two fire extinguishers duly approved by Fire Team.

Question: For which excavations is an Excavation Notification required under KOC.SA.004?
Reference: Cl. 5.13.6: an Excavation Notification is required for all excavations regardless of the depth.

Question: A NORM survey before vessel cleaning gives a dose rate of 4 µSv/hr. How is the location classified?
Reference: Cl. 5.23: 0.5–10 µSv/hr = Supervised Area (hourly readings); above 10 µSv/hr = Controlled Area and work stopped.

Question: During a routine check, an SCBA breathing air cylinder gauge shows it has dropped below full charge. At what point does KOC.SA.005 require it to be sent for recharging?
A: When pressure falls to 90% of the specified pressure
B: When pressure falls to 75% of the specified pressure
C: When pressure falls to 50% of the specified pressure
Reference: Cl. 4.2 / 5.4.3: cylinder pressure must not be less than 90% of full capacity; refill when pressure drops to 90% of specified pressure.

Question: When checking an SCBA, the cylinder valve is closed slowly to test the low-pressure warning alarm. At approximately what level of cylinder capacity should the alarm sound?
Reference: Cl. 5.4.5 C: verify activation of the low pressure alarm (to sound at approximately 25% of cylinder capacity).

Question: What is the maximum validity of an RPE 'Authorized User Card' issued by the Controlling Team?
Reference: Cl. 5.4.4: validity of the Authorized User Card shall not exceed 12 months and must be within the medical examination validity.

Question: What periodic hydrostatic test intervals does KOC.SA.005 specify for SCBA breathing air cylinders?
A: Steel every 3 years; composite every 5 years
B: Steel every 5 years; composite every 3 years
C: Steel and composite both every 5 years
D: Steel and composite both every 10 years
Reference: Cl. 5.4.5 C: verify SCBA cylinder is current on hydrostatic test (5 years for steel, 3 years for composite cylinders).

Question: A worker passes a quantitative fit test with a full-face respirator. Which requirement then applies on the job?
A: Any model from the same manufacturer may be used
B: Any size of the same model may be used
C: The exact same make, model, style and size must be used
D: Any tight-fitting respirator with the same APF may be used
Reference: Cl. 5.7: after passing a fit test, the user must use the exact same make, model, style and size of respirator; fit testing is at least annual.

Question: What minimum specification does KOC.SA.005 set for SCBA used by emergency services (Fire Group)?
A: Negative pressure type, minimum 30 minutes duration
B: Positive pressure type, minimum 30 minutes duration
C: Positive pressure type, minimum 45 minutes duration
D: Positive pressure type, minimum 60 minutes duration
Reference: Cl. 5.2.1 Note 1: SCBA for emergency services shall be positive pressure type with minimum 45 minutes duration, conforming to NFPA 1981.

Question: An air-purifying respirator filter has been removed from its sealed packaging but rarely used. When must it be replaced, regardless of use?
Reference: Cl. 5.4.5 B: a filter once opened from the seal must be replaced after 6 months regardless of its use.

Question: How often, at a minimum, must the output air quality of a breathing air compressor be checked?
A: Every month, and after each filter change
B: Every 3 months, and after each filter change
C: Every 6 months, and after each filter change
D: Every 12 months, and after each filter change
Reference: Cl. 5.9: periodic checks of compressor output air quality at least once every 3 months and after each filter change.

Question: For KOC.SA.005, an atmosphere is oxygen deficient (and treated as IDLH) when oxygen is below:
Reference: Cl. 2.0: oxygen deficient atmosphere — less than 19.5% oxygen by volume; treated as IDLH for this procedure.

Question: What must a wearer of a tight-fitting respirator do to ensure an adequate face seal?
A: Apply barrier cream to the face
C: Wear a cap under the head straps
D: Be clean shaven where the mask seals
Reference: Cl. 4.6: all tight-fitting respirator wearers shall, according to manufacturer's instructions, be clean shaven.

Question: Excluding escape-only sets, what is the minimum number of SCBA wearers that must be present when SCBA is used for work?
Reference: Cl. 4.6: SCBA/SAR users shall ensure a minimum of two SCBA wearers are present, with standby crew and an SCBA Controller.

Question: For what purpose may an escape-only respirator be used?
Reference: Cl. 5.4.5: escape-only respirators must not be used for re-entry or work; they are for emergency exit only.

Question: A quantitative fit test gives a fit factor of 100. What does this mean?
A: The mask is rated for use up to 100 ppm
B: The mask lets in 100% of the outside air
C: The mask may be worn for 100 minutes
D: Air inside is 100 times cleaner than outside
Reference: Cl. 2.0 Note: a fit factor of 100 means that the air inside the respirator is 100 times cleaner than the air outside.

Question: How often must respirators maintained for emergency use be inspected by the Fire (Support Services) Team?
Reference: Cl. 5.4.5 table: respirators for emergency situations — at least monthly and checked before and after each use.

Question: During inspection, the foil seal of an air-purifying escape respirator (APER) is found broken. What must be done?
A: Reseal the pouch with tape and keep it
B: Take it out of service and dispose of it
C: Return it to stock after a visual check
D: Use it for training sessions only
Reference: Cl. 5.4.5 A: if the foil seal has been broken, the APER must be taken out of service and disposed of.

Question: What is the normal duration of an escape-only respirator as defined in KOC.SA.005?
Reference: Cl. 2.0: escape-only respirator — SCBA or APER type, normally 15 minutes duration.

Question: How should an SCBA set be stored when not in use?
A: Cylinder valve closed, harness straps fully extended
B: Cylinder valve open, straps fully tightened
C: Facepiece fitted to the regulator under pressure
D: Cylinder partly charged to reduce stress
Reference: Cl. 5.4.3: SCBA stored with cylinder valves closed; harness straps adjusted to maximum length; cylinders stored fully charged.

Question: Under the breathing air quality limits in KOC.SA.005 (NFPA 1989), the maximum carbon monoxide content is:
Reference: Cl. 5.9 table: carbon monoxide up to 5 ppm; CO2 up to 1000 ppm; oxygen 19.5–23.5%.

Question: How often must RPE authorized users attend refresher training?
C: Only when the card is lost
Reference: Cl. 5.4.4: training must recur at least annually; RPE wearers shall undergo refresher training annually.

Question: What minimum percentage of third-party SCBA inspection and servicing must be witnessed or verified by the Controlling Team?
Reference: Cl. 4.1 / 4.2: at least 5% of inspection / servicing by third parties shall be witnessed / verified by the Controlling Team.

Question: What distinguishes a positive pressure respirator under KOC.SA.005?
B: Air is drawn through a filter cartridge
C: Facepiece pressure goes negative on inhalation
D: It is designed for escape use only
Reference: Cl. 2.0: positive pressure respirator — pressure inside the facepiece is positive during both inhalation and exhalation.

Question: Which set of gas test results permits confined space entry WITHOUT respiratory protection under KOC.SA.007 Table 1?
Reference: Table 1: entry without respiratory protection when O2 is 19.5–23.5%, flammables < 10% LEL and H2S < 10 ppm.

Question: Gas testing of a vessel shows 15% oxygen. According to KOC.SA.007 Table 1, what is the correct action?
A: Entry permitted with an air-purifying respirator
B: Entry permitted with forced ventilation only
C: Entry permitted with SCBA and continuous monitoring
D: No entry, except in an emergency or for rescue
Reference: Table 1: oxygen content less than 16% (or H2S > 100 ppm, or flammables 50% LEL or above) = NO ENTRY except emergency or rescue.

Question: The initial confined space gas test was done at 08:00 but entry is delayed until 09:15. What does KOC.SA.007 require?
A: Entry may proceed because the test is valid for the shift
B: A follow-up gas test by the Worksite Supervisor before entry
C: A new Confined Space Entry Certificate must be raised
D: Entry may proceed if entrants wear personal H2S monitors
Reference: Cl. 5.3: entry is to take place within one hour of the initial gas test; otherwise a follow-up gas test by the Worksite Supervisor is required before entry.

Question: Where periodic (rather than continuous) gas monitoring is used during a confined space entry, the interval between tests shall not exceed:
Reference: Cl. 5.13: the periodic monitoring of gas shall not exceed a two-hour period.

Question: How frequently does KOC.SA.007 require personnel working inside a vessel or tank to be given a rest period, unless conditions require more frequent breaks?
Reference: Cl. 5.11: personnel working inside the vessel / tank will be given a rest period at each 30 minute interval, or more frequently.

Question: Inside a KOC hydrocarbon facility, an excavation is classified as a confined space when its depth exceeds:
Reference: Cl. 2.0 c): excavation with depth more than 1.2 m inside hydrocarbon facilities is a confined space.

Question: An entrant collapses inside a vessel. What is the correct immediate action for the standby person who is not trained in search and rescue?
A: Enter at once wearing an escape set and pull the entrant out
B: Summon aid via the Control Room and stay outside until relief arrives
C: Send another entrant inside to assist the casualty to the manway
D: Lower a spare SCBA set to the casualty and wait at the manway
Reference: Cl. 4.4 Note / 5.11: the standby person must not enter until relief arrives; he must summon aid immediately via the Control Room.

Question: Which of the following must NEVER be used to ventilate a confined space?
Reference: Cl. 5.5: compressed oxygen or instrument air shall never be used to ventilate a confined space.

Question: A vessel has been certified gas free but flammable residues may remain. If extra-low-voltage portable lighting is used, what is its maximum voltage under KOC.SA.007?
Reference: Cl. 5.6: such spaces may be illuminated by extra low voltage (25 V AC) portable lighting approved for Zone 1; transformers never taken inside.

Question: When is a person considered to have 'entered' a confined space?
A: Only when work actually starts inside
B: Only after passing 1 m beyond the manway
C: Only when the whole body is inside the space
D: When any part, even just the head, is inside
Reference: Cl. 2.0 / 5.4: confined space entry covers complete body entry and also when only the head is inserted.

Question: Which sign is displayed at an approved confined space entry point while the standby person is present?
A: Red: no entry to this confined space at all
B: Yellow: caution, gas testing now in progress
C: Blue: breathing apparatus must be worn inside
D: Green: entry allowed with permit and standby
Reference: Cl. 5.4: 'ENTRY ALLOWED WITH PERMIT IN THE PRESENCE OF STANDBY PERSON' (green background, white font) at approved entry points.

Question: How often must a Confined Space Entry Certificate be re-endorsed?
D: Only at change of work party
Reference: Cl. 5.4: the Confined Space Entry Certificate must be re-endorsed by each shift.

Question: Before personnel enter a vessel, how must it be isolated from connected lines?
A: Stopping, locking and tagging the feed pump
B: Closing the nearest block valve and tagging it
C: Closing two valves and opening the bleed between
D: Spool removal or rated spades near the vessel
Reference: Cl. 5.2.1: isolation as close as possible to the vessel by physical disconnection or spades/spectacle blinds of the same pressure rating as the flange.

Question: During atmospheric venting of a vessel, H2S in the workers' breathing zone exceeds 10 ppm. What must be done?
A: Move workers 5 m away and continue
B: Issue escape sets and continue venting
C: Continue venting at a slower rate
D: Stop venting and remove the source first
Reference: Cl. 5.2.2: if H2S exceeds 10 ppm in the breathing zone, stop venting and flush/purge or eliminate the source before resuming.

Question: Why is a probe extension used when testing the atmosphere inside a vessel after opening the manway?
A: To keep the gas detector sensors dry
B: To sample inside, not just near the entry
C: To raise the detector's alarm set points
D: To test the air just outside the vessel
Reference: Cl. 5.3: a probe extension shall be used so that the atmosphere within the vessel is sampled and not the region close to entry.

Question: What respiratory protection is required to enter a vessel that still contains sludge or residue?
B: SCBA or airline unit at all times
C: None if the gas test is satisfactory
Reference: Table 1 Note 2: entry into a vessel having sludge or residue shall be permitted only wearing SCBA / airline unit all the time.

Question: Which equipment shall NOT be used for initial air purging of a vessel that contained hydrocarbons?
Reference: Cl. 5.2.5: electrically driven air movers shall not be used for initial air purging; only at a later stage after gas tests confirm.

Question: For welding or cutting inside a confined space, where must compressed gas cylinders be kept?
A: Inside, secured to the vessel wall
D: Inside, if fitted with flashback arrestors
Reference: Cl. 5.8: compressed gas cylinders shall not be allowed in a confined space for welding or cutting activities.

Question: What must the standby person do each time personnel enter or leave the vessel?
A: Record it at the end of the shift
B: Inform the Fire Station by phone
C: Inform the Control Room by radio
D: Tell the Permit Issuer in person
Reference: Cl. 5.11: the standby person informs the Control Room by radio each time the vessel is entered or vacated; logged in the Control Room logbook.

Question: Entrants must wear SCBA because hydrocarbons are present inside a vessel. Which tools may they use?
Reference: Cl. 5.7: if SCBA is required due to hydrocarbons, no electrical tools; only pneumatically driven tools; no spark-generating tools.

Question: How must pyrophoric sludge be handled during vessel cleaning?
A: Scraped out dry using steel tools
B: Allowed to dry fully before removal
C: Left in place until the shutdown ends
D: Kept wet and removed as soon as possible
Reference: Cl. 5.10: pyrophoric sludge shall be kept wet and taken out of the vessel as soon as possible and disposed of safely.

Question: Why must entrants into a sewer wear SCBA or an airline unit at all times?
A: Sewers have no means of exit
C: Gas detectors do not work in sewers
D: Sewers can rarely be fully isolated
Reference: Table 1 Note 3: sewers rarely can be completely isolated; the atmosphere may pose unpredictable toxic or flammable hazards.

Question: On a bench-mounted grinder, what is the maximum gap permitted between the work rest and the abrasive wheel?
Reference: Cl. 5.1.2.1: work rest adjusted as close to the wheel as possible at a maximum distance of 1/4 inch.

Question: The 'ring test' described in KOC.SA.012 for checking an abrasive wheel for cracks is applicable to which type of wheel?
B: Small wheels of 100 mm diameter or less
Reference: Cl. 5.1.2.3 / 5.1.2.5: the ring test is used only for vitrified bonded wheels; it is not practicable for small, mounted, segment or plate-mounted wheels.

Question: After a new abrasive wheel is mounted, how long should it be allowed to run free, with users standing clear, before use?
Reference: Cl. 5.1.2.3: new wheels should be allowed to run free for about 60 seconds; users should stand clear.

Question: A technician is selecting a cutting disc for a portable grinder. Which speed rating requirement must the disc meet?
A: Rated at or above the RPM of the grinder
B: Rated at 75% of the grinder RPM
C: Rated below the grinder RPM to reduce vibration
D: Any rating, provided a speed governor is fitted
Reference: Cl. 5.1.2.1: ensure speed of the wheel is compatible with the machine, i.e. use a wheel or disc rated at or above the RPM of the grinder.

Question: Under KOC.SA.012, a mobile air compressor may be deployed in a Zone 2 hazardous area only:
A: Under a Cold Work Permit with continuous gas monitoring
B: Under a Hot Work Permit, if suitable for the area classification
C: Under a Vehicle Entry Permit, if a spark arrestor is fitted
D: It is never permitted in a Zone 2 area
Reference: Cl. 5.2.2: mobile compressors are not permitted in Zone 0 & 1; in Zone 2 they must be covered by an authorized Hot Work Permit, subject to suitability.

Question: Which method of connecting a pneumatic tool to its high-pressure air hose is acceptable under KOC.SA.012?
A: Screw-adjusted 'Jubilee' clip, tightened with a screwdriver
B: Crowfoot coupling with retaining pin/clip and whip check
C: Wire-twisted joint secured with heavy-duty insulation tape
D: Push-fit coupling, with the hose tied to the tool handle
Reference: Cl. 5.2.1 / 5.2.3: purpose-made connections (e.g. crowfoot) with retaining pin/clip and whip; 'Jubilee' type connections are not permitted.

Question: At or above what noise level from air compressors and pneumatic tools must warning signs be displayed and hearing protection worn?
Reference: Cl. 5.2.1: if noise levels are at or above 85 dB, signs must be displayed and hearing protection worn.

Question: Abrasive wheels in a store have been in stock for more than two years. What does KOC.SA.012 recommend before they are issued?
A: Issue them only for light grinding work
B: Consult the manufacturer or supplier first
C: Ring test them all, including resin wheels
D: Discard them without any further assessment
Reference: Cl. 5.1.2.7: in case of doubt, or if wheels have been in stock for more than two years, the manufacturer/supplier should be consulted.

Question: Under KOC.SA.012, how quickly can a Ground Fault Circuit Interrupter (GFCI) shut off power after a ground fault?
Reference: Cl. 2.0: a GFCI is designed to shut off power in the event of a ground fault within as little as 1/40 of a second.

Question: How is a double-insulated portable electric tool identified?
C: A lightning bolt in a circle
Reference: Cl. 2.0: double-insulated tools are marked with the double insulation symbol (a square within a square).

Question: Which gas must NEVER be used to power pneumatic tools?
A: Compressed air from a plant compressor
C: Compressed air from a mobile compressor
Reference: Cl. 5.2.3: never use oxygen in pneumatic tools, as oil and gas pressure friction can cause fire or explosion.

Question: Why must instrument air NOT be used to operate pneumatic tools?
B: It is too dry to lubricate the tool
C: It is always above tool rated pressure
D: Pressure dips could upset the plant
Reference: Cl. 5.2.1: instrument air must not be used for pneumatic tools to avoid abnormality or upset in plant condition due to pressure variation.

Question: An operator finds that a grinder is defective. What should he do?
A: Tag it 'Defective – Don't Use' and report it
B: Use it carefully until the job ends
C: Return it to the store without reporting
D: Repair it on site with spare parts
Reference: Cl. 5.1.2.6: remove it from service, tag it 'Defective-Don't USE', and report the problem to the supervisor.

Question: How often must the Controlling Team's inspection programme check abrasive wheel equipment?
A: Monthly, plus daily user visual checks
D: Weekly, with no checks by the users
Reference: Cl. 5.1.2.6: abrasive wheel equipment subject to a monthly inspection programme; users inspect visually daily before use.

Question: Which statement about the trigger of a pneumatic tool is correct?
A: It may be tied down if two people operate it
B: It must not lock 'on'; dead-man never bypassed
C: Its dead-man switch may be bypassed if guarded
D: It may be locked 'on' for long cutting jobs
Reference: Cl. 5.2.3: only finger-operated switches; the tool must not be usable with the trigger locked; dead-man switch never bypassed.

Question: Where must batteries of battery-operated tools NOT be removed or replaced?
Reference: Cl. 5.3.2: batteries must not be removed / replaced in hazardous areas.

Question: Which use of compressed air is prohibited under KOC.SA.012?
A: Running an air impact wrench on bolts
B: Blowing dust off a person's clothing
C: Powering an approved portable air pump
D: Driving an air-powered drill on a job
Reference: Cl. 5.2.3: compressed air should not be used for cleaning dust from the body; exhaust air directed away from the body.

Question: How should organic (resin) bonded abrasive wheels be stored to prevent warping?
A: On edge in a cradle in direct sunlight
B: Stacked in a damp room to stay soft
C: Flat on a steel surface, away from heat
D: Hung on hooks through the centre hole
Reference: Cl. 5.1.2.7: organic bonded wheels should be laid flat on a horizontal steel surface away from excessive heat and moisture.

Question: What should be drained from the air receiver, intercooler and aftercooler at the end of each day?
Reference: Cl. 5.2.2: at the end of each day, any accumulation of oil and water should be drained from the air receiver, intercooler, aftercooler and supply pipes.

Question: What is the correct way to disconnect a portable electric tool from a socket?
A: Switch off at the tool and leave it plugged in
B: Pull the plug, not the cord
C: Cut the cord near the plug
Reference: Cl. 5.3.1: pull the plug, not the cord; pulling the cord causes wear and may cause electric shock.

Question: What is the maximum age of a contractor's mobile equipment or heavy vehicle permitted for work in KOC business under KOC.SA.013?
Reference: Cl. 5.2: contractor mobile equipment / heavy vehicles shall not be older than 20 years, subject to suitability and 3rd party certification.

Question: How often must a contractor's mobile crane (load handling equipment) be inspected and certified by a KOC-approved inspection contractor?
C: Every 12 months or contract duration, whichever is earlier
Reference: Cl. 5.4 I a): general mobile equipment once a year (or contract duration if earlier); load or material handling equipment once every 6 months per KOC.SA.029.

Question: A contractor's forklift is involved in a minor incident and then repaired. What does KOC.SA.013 require before it is used again?
A: The operator completes a pre-use checklist
B: A new Clearance Certificate based on a new inspection report
C: The existing Clearance Certificate is endorsed by the Area HSE Team
D: No action is needed for a minor incident
Reference: Cl. 4.6: after any incident or major repair / modification, a new Clearance Certificate is issued based on a new inspection report from a KOC-approved inspection contractor.

Question: Under KOC.SA.013, gasoline-operated equipment such as a jumping compactor is restricted on site unless it is fitted with:
A: A reverse alarm and a reverse camera
B: Vibration-resistant fuel caps and spark arrestors
D: A dead-man switch and emergency stop button
Reference: Cl. 4.6: gasoline-operated equipment is restricted unless fitted with vibration-resistant fuel caps and spark arrestors.

Question: In which areas does KOC.SA.013 require mobile equipment to hold a valid Clearance Certificate?
A: Only in Zone 0 and Zone 1 hazardous areas
B: Only in hazardous areas inside plant fences
C: In both hazardous and non-hazardous areas
D: Only for equipment with a State registration plate
Reference: Cl. 5.1: all mobile equipment shall require a Clearance Certificate for both hazardous and non-hazardous areas including Ahmadi area.

Question: A contractor wants to move a generator from Contract A to Contract B, both under the same contractor, using Contract A's Clearance Certificate and Gate Pass. Under KOC.SA.013 this is:
A: Acceptable, since the contractor is the same
B: Acceptable, if the certificate is still valid
C: Not acceptable; it must be issued under Contract B
Reference: Cl. 4.6: contractor cannot use mobile equipment with another contract's Clearance Certificate and Gate Pass, even if the contractor is the same (drilling teams excepted).

Question: During maintenance on a dump truck with a raised bed, which control does KOC.SA.013 require to protect personnel?
A: Lowering the bed onto stacked timber blocks
B: Fitting a mechanical locking device to the raised bed
C: Keeping the engine running so hydraulics hold the bed
D: Posting a banksman to watch the bed during work
Reference: Cl. 5.1.1 (2): no personnel under a raised bed; use appropriate mechanical locking devices during maintenance to prevent sudden bed movement.

Question: Which precaution must be met before a heavy vehicle without an inbuilt spark arrestor is deployed at a KOC worksite?
A: Its exhaust tail pipe must be fitted with a spark arrestor
B: It must be parked at least 30 m from process equipment
C: Its engine must be switched off every 30 minutes
D: Its fuel tank must be at least half full
Reference: Cl. 5.1.1: the exhaust tail pipe is fitted with a spark arrestor in case it is not inbuilt.

Question: How often must general mobile equipment (not load-handling) be inspected and certified by a KOC-approved inspection contractor?
C: Yearly, or contract period if earlier
Reference: Cl. 5.4 I a): inspection and certification once a year or for the duration of the contract, whichever is earlier (load handling: every 6 months).

Question: Under KOC.SA.013, the Security Team issues a Gate Pass for mobile equipment only after it has:
A: A Clearance Certificate from the Controlling Team
B: A fuel receipt issued by the contractor's office
C: A verbal OK from the driver's own supervisor
D: A photograph of the equipment taken at the gate
Reference: Cl. 4.3 / 5.4 VI: Security issues the gate pass only after ensuring the equipment has a Clearance Certificate.

Question: Which warning device must mobile equipment have to protect people behind it while reversing?
A: A horn fitted on the trailer only
C: A blue flashing light on the roof
Reference: Cl. 5.1.1: mobile equipment shall be equipped with a reverse alarm clearly audible to warn persons behind.

Question: Besides a reverse alarm, what additional device does KOC.SA.013 require on mobile equipment and heavy vehicles?
Reference: Cl. 5.1.1: mobile equipment and heavy vehicles shall be equipped with a reverse camera system.

Question: During certification, the inspection finds a non-conformance with the Safety Checklist. What concession may the certifying team give?
A: A concession if the contractor signs an undertaking
B: No concession on any checklist item
D: A concession for non-critical items only
Reference: Cl. 5.4 V: certifying teams shall in no case give any concession related to non-conformance on any aspect of the safety checklist.

Question: What applies to an in-built non-intrinsically safe radio/music system in a vehicle working in a hazardous area?
A: It may be used if windows are closed
B: It shall not be switched on or off
C: It may be used at low volume
D: It may be used outside Zone 1
Reference: Cl. 5.1.1: inbuilt non-intrinsically safe transistor / music system shall not be activated (turned on or off).

Question: What must be done with an in-built cigarette lighter in mobile equipment before deployment at a KOC worksite?
A: Replace it with a USB charger
B: Remove it from the power output
C: Leave it but post a 'No Smoking' sign
Reference: Cl. 5.1.1: in-built cigarette lighter(s) / any other devices are removed from the power output.

Question: Under the 2026 revision, who must the contractor appoint as focal point for maintenance, repairs and operators' equipment concerns?
Reference: Cl. 4.6: contractor shall assign an Equipment Coordinator responsible for prompt maintenance and repairs and as focal point for operators.

Question: When must a heavy equipment operator complete the daily operator checklist?
A: Once a week, on the rest day
B: At the end of each working shift
Reference: Cl. 4.6: heavy equipment operator to inspect and fill in the daily operator checklist before start of the work.

Question: Which of the following mobile equipment requires third-party test certification under KOC.SA.013?
Reference: Cl. 5.4 II b): equipment fitted with safety valves (e.g. air compressor) requires 3rd party test certification.

Question: How long must Clearance Certificates for mobile equipment be retained if there were no incidents?
A: 2 years from the date of expiry
C: Until the contract is closed out
D: 1 year from the date of issue
Reference: Cl. 8.0: Clearance Certificates — minimum 5 years from date of expiry if no incidents; otherwise indefinite.

Question: During unloading by a dump truck, what control does KOC.SA.013 require around the truck?
A: A banksman standing behind the bed
B: Only a horn signal before tipping
C: Workers guiding the load by hand
Reference: Cl. 5.1.1 (2): establish and maintain a safe exclusion zone during unloading and install proper barricades.

Question: In-service flange bolting replacement (hot bolting) is NOT permitted on flanges having fewer than how many bolts?
Reference: Cl. 5.3: in-service bolt replacement / rework is not permitted on flanges with less than six bolts.

Question: Above what line pressure does KOC.SA.015 prohibit in-service flange bolting replacement?
Reference: Cl. 5.3: not permitted on high-pressure lines > 13.6 bar (200 psi) including air, nitrogen and hydrocarbons.

Question: A gas line contains 800 ppm of H2S. Under KOC.SA.015, can in-service hot bolting be carried out on it?
A: Yes, if all workers wear SCBA
B: Yes, if line pressure is first reduced
C: No, it is in highly sour service
D: No, any line above 10 ppm is excluded
Reference: Cl. 2.0 / 5.3: highly sour service is > 500 ppm H2S; hot bolting is not permitted on systems in highly sour service.

Question: During in-service bolt replacement on a live flange, how many bolts may be slackened at any one time?
D: Up to one quarter of the bolts
Reference: Cl. 5.3 d): slacken one bolt only; under no circumstances must two bolts be slackened at any one time.

Question: When fitting new bolts during in-service bolt replacement (without tensioning equipment), how far may the bolt protrude beyond the nut?
B: No more than two full threads
C: No more than five full threads
Reference: Cl. 5.3 h): new bolts should protrude no more than two full threads beyond the nut.

Question: While breaking a flange, the crew finds the bolts are badly corroded and will not turn. What is the only acceptable removal method under KOC.SA.015?
A: Gas cutting with an oxy-acetylene torch
D: Striking the nuts with an iron hammer
Reference: Cl. 5.4: if bolts are corroded, the only acceptable method is a pneumatic hacksaw; gas cutting (open flame) shall not be used.

Question: What is the correct body position and first bolt to loosen when breaking a flange that may still contain pressure?
A: Stand downwind and loosen the bolts nearest to you
B: Stand upwind and loosen the bolts farthest away from you
C: Stand directly in front and loosen bolts clockwise
D: Stand upwind and loosen all bolts evenly at the same time
Reference: Cl. 5.2 o) / 5.5 a): maintain a safe upwind position and loosen bolts farthest away first so any release sprays away from the worker.

Question: Which type of hammer may be used when breaking flanges on lines in hydrocarbon service?
D: Any hammer, if a fire watch is present
Reference: Cl. 5.4: do not use an iron hammer in hydrocarbon service because impact will generate sparks; only brass hammers shall be used.

Question: What is the minimum number of persons required for a flange break under KOC.SA.015?
Reference: Cl. 5.2 n): 'Flange Break' is a two-person task; two or more persons work together at all times.

Question: Who positively identifies, by suitable tagging, all flanges to be broken during the site survey?
Reference: Cl. 4.1 / 5.1: the Work Permit Issuer conducts a site survey and positively identifies (by tagging) all flanges to be broken.

Question: In-service bolt replacement is NOT permitted on systems operating at which temperatures?
Reference: Cl. 5.3: not permitted on systems operating below 0°C and in excess of 60°C.

Question: Who approves the 'In-Service Flange Bolting Replacement / Rework Request Form' (KOC/IS/01)?
A: Completed by Permit Applicant, approved by Permit Issuer
B: Completed by HSE Officer, approved by Controlling Team
C: Completed by Permit Issuer, approved by Asset HSE Team
D: Completed by the fitter, approved by his own supervisor
Reference: Cl. 5.3: KOC/IS/01 must be completed by the Permit Applicant and approved by the Permit Issuer.

Question: Which bolts must be used when reinstating a flange under KOC.SA.015?
A: Any bolts available in the site store
C: Machine bolts of any available rating
D: Bolts and nuts of correct size and rating
Reference: Cl. 4.2: ensure that machine bolts are not used, rather bolts and nuts of appropriate size and rating are used.

Question: A fitter wants to slip a pipe over his spanner for extra leverage on a seized bolt. Under KOC.SA.015 this is:
A: Permitted with a second person holding
B: Permitted if the pipe is short
D: Not permitted, due to slippage injury
Reference: Cl. 5.2 j): modification of tools by using additional pipe / cheater bar for extra leverage is not permitted.

Question: During hot bolting, may a corroded bolt be removed by burning or grinding?
A: Yes, under a Hot Work Permit
B: No, hot cutting is not permitted
C: Yes, if the line is below 13.6 bar
D: Yes, with a fire watch present
Reference: Cl. 5.3: bolt cutting by any hot methods, including burning and grinding, is not permitted during hot bolting operations.

Question: After one bolt has been replaced during hot bolting, which bolt should be slackened next?
Reference: Cl. 5.3 j): proceed to slacken the next bolt diagonally opposite to the one just replaced.

Question: A leak occurs while workers wearing breathing air masks are breaking a flange. What should they do?
A: Keep masks on and evacuate per the plan
B: Tighten the bolts before they leave
C: Stay at the flange and await orders
Reference: Cl. 5.2 g): workers must not remove their breathing air mask in case of leak; they must follow the emergency plan.

Question: Before loosening any flange bolt, how must line depressurization be confirmed?
A: Tap the pipe and listen for gas
B: Read the control room pressure only
C: Ask the operator for verbal confirmation
D: Crack open a nearby drain, vent or gauge
Reference: Cl. 5.2 e) / 5.4: depressurization confirmed by crack opening a drain / vent, instrument tapping or pressure gauge.

Question: Lines containing hydrocarbons are being re-worked in an area. Under KOC.SA.015, other Hot Work in the same area is:
Reference: Cl. 5.2 m): no other 'Hot Work' is allowed in the same area where lines containing hydrocarbons are being replaced / re-worked.

Question: When may a bolt be completely removed while breaking a flange?
A: After the two top bolts have been slackened
B: At any time, provided the line is drained
C: Only when all are slack and the flange is apart
D: As soon as the first bolt turns freely
Reference: Cl. 5.4: do not completely remove any bolt until all of the bolts have been slackened and the flange is apart.

Question: A leak clamp has been installed on a process line. Within what period does KOC.SA.017 require the original integrity of the line to be restored?
Reference: Cl. 5.2: all clamps are temporary; appropriate actions shall be taken to restore original integrity within three months.

Question: If permanent repair cannot be done within the initial period, a Clamp Joint Evaluation Meeting may authorize the clamp for a further maximum of:
Reference: Cl. 5.2 / 5.3: the Asset Owner may request extension through the Clamp Joint Evaluation Meeting for a maximum of six months after the initial three months.

Question: How far in advance must the Asset Owner submit a Clamp Extension Request, with valid justification, before the agreed clamp period expires?
Reference: Cl. 5.4: request shall be submitted at least ten working days prior to exceeding the agreed period; authorization from Group Manager (Ops/GO).

Question: Inspection finds that the leak on a pipeline is caused by a crack. What does KOC.SA.017 require?
A: Fit a bolt-on mechanical clamp rated for the MAOP
B: Fit a sealing band clamp centred on the crack
C: Do not clamp; replace the cracked spool with new pipe
D: Fit a split sleeve clamp and de-rate the line
Reference: Cl. 5.2: if a crack appears on any area of the piping, clamping shall not be used; the cracked portion shall be replaced with a new pipe spool.

Question: What pressure capability must a bolt-on mechanical leak clamp have under KOC.SA.017?
A: At least 50% of the line's operating pressure
B: At least equal to the normal operating pressure only
C: Capable of containing the MAOP of the carrier pipe
D: Equal to the hydrotest pressure of the clamp only
Reference: Cl. 4.3 / 5.2: clamp design pressure not less than that of the piping; the clamp must be capable of containing the MAOP of the carrier pipe.

Question: When sealing band clamps are used on isolated external corrosion pits, what is the minimum spacing between two such clamps?
A: No two clamps within one pipe diameter of each other
B: No two clamps within 0.5 m of each other
C: No two clamps within three pipe diameters of each other
D: No minimum spacing applies between clamps
Reference: Cl. 5.2: no two such clamps shall be installed within one pipe diameter of each other.

Question: When a pipeline leak occurs at a KOC facility, to whom must it be reported in the first instance under KOC.SA.017?
C: Asset PSM Team within 10 working days
D: Contracts Group through the Clamp Register
Reference: Cl. 5.1: whenever a leak occurs it shall be reported to ERCU at 160 and all concerned per KOC.GE.007.

Question: A pipeline leak is caused by general corrosion and shows signs of multiple leaks. Which repair means should be considered first?
A: A sealing band clamp at each leak point
C: Epoxy wrap over the corroded area
D: A bolt-on clamp on the largest leak only
Reference: Cl. 5.2: clamps are for localized pitting leaks; for general corrosion with multiple leaks, a split sleeve clamp should be considered first.

Question: How must a pipeline operating with a leak clamp in position be regarded?
A: As fully repaired and safe to operate normally
B: As permanently restored once 3 months pass
C: As under repair; operating it is a last option
D: As safe, if the clamp is rated for the MAOP
Reference: Cl. 1.0: clamped piping shall be considered as under repair, regarded as unsafe; operating with a clamp is a last option.

Question: Within how many working days must Operations inform Maintenance, HSE, PSM and I&C teams of a leak incident?
Reference: Cl. 4.1: inform all concerned teams about the leak incident within ten working days from the date of leak.

Question: How often must the Clamp Register be updated through joint site inspections and circulated?
Reference: Cl. 4.1: maintain and update the clamp register monthly through joint site inspections and circulate monthly.

Question: How often is the summary report of clamp status in each facility released to PSM, HSE, Maintenance and I&C teams?
Reference: Cl. 4.1 / 4.6: release the quarterly report of clamp status in each facility (Appendix III).

Question: For a sealing band clamp on an isolated corrosion pit, what minimum remaining wall thickness is required within one pipe diameter of the pit?
Reference: Cl. 5.2: no portion within the one-diameter region shall have minimum remaining wall thickness less than 20% of nominal.

Question: How should a clamped location on an underground pipeline be managed after clamping?
A: Left exposed where possible and barricaded
B: Painted and buried with a marker post
C: Covered with steel plates and left
Reference: Cl. 5.5: clamped underground locations shall not be backfilled if possible; exposed locations barricaded with warning signs.

Question: Who authorizes a clamp to remain beyond the agreed period, after a Clamp Extension Request meeting?
Reference: Cl. 5.4: authorization for the extension shall be taken from the Group Manager (Ops/GO).

Question: On which pipework shall clamps NOT be installed?
B: Pipe with a single isolated pit
D: Water lines with a pinhole leak
Reference: Cl. 5.2: clamps shall not be installed on severely deformed or corroded (externally) piping / pipelines.

Question: A clamp has passed the end of its approved extension period. How is it classified?
Reference: Cl. 5.4 Note: if a clamp exceeds the extension period, it is considered an overdue clamp.

Question: Which team issues recommendations (Inspection Action Report) for permanent repair of a leaked pipeline?
Reference: Cl. 4.2: Inspection & Corrosion Teams issue recommendations (Inspection Action Report or Memorandum) for permanent repairs.

Question: Which team is responsible for selecting and installing the approved leak clamp?
Reference: Cl. 4.3: Maintenance / Gas Maintenance responsible for selection and installation of the approved clamp.

Question: If a clamped line must be operated at de-rated parameters, which procedure must be followed?
Reference: Cl. 5.5: de-rated parameters shall be implemented through the Management of Change Procedure KOC.GE.006.

Question: What minimum horizontal radius of warning barricade does KOC.SA.019 require around a hot-tapping site?
Reference: Cl. 5.3.1 xxii: hot-tapping site shall have a warning barricade with a horizontal radius not less than 15 m; mobile equipment kept upwind outside it.

Question: When a line packer or seal plug is used, how must the end of its vent pipe be arranged?
A: At least 15 m away and left open to atmosphere
B: At least 30 m away and dipped in a water bucket
C: At least 30 m away and connected to the flare
D: At least 50 m away and fitted with an end cap
Reference: Cl. 4.4 / 5.3.3: vent pipe end kept at least 30 m away, dipped in a bucket of clear water, monitored continuously; stop work if bubbles appear.

Question: Under KOC.SA.019, for which activity is the signature of the KOC Inspection Engineer required on the work permit?
D: All hot-tapping, welding and plugging work
Reference: Cl. 4.2: Inspection Engineer approval is required only for in-service welding, after confirming remaining wall thickness.

Question: How should the hot-tapping machine be installed with respect to the operator's position?
A: So the operator stands downwind of the machine
B: So the operator stands upwind of the machine
C: So the operator stands directly above the cutter
D: Wind direction is not a consideration
Reference: Cl. 4.4: ensure the hot-tapping machine is installed in such a way that the operator is positioned in the upwind direction.

Question: How must the weight of the hot-tapping machine be managed during the operation?
A: Rest fully on the pipeline being tapped
B: Be independently supported off the pipeline
C: Be held by a crane throughout the operation
D: Be supported on scaffolding tied to the pipe
Reference: Cl. 5.3.1 xix: the hot-tapping machine shall be independently supported; its weight shall not be transferred to the equipment being tapped.

Question: Which statement about sparking tools is correct under KOC.SA.019?
A: They are prohibited during both hot-tapping and welding
B: They are allowed during hot-tapping but not during welding
C: They are not allowed during hot-tapping but are allowed during welding
D: They are allowed during both if a fire watch is present
Reference: Cl. 5.3.1 xviii: sparking tools shall not be used during hot tapping; however, they are allowed during welding.

Question: During a plugging operation, which step is designated a 'HOLD POINT' to be witnessed by the Company's representative?
Reference: Cl. 5.3.3: installation of the gas plug shall be a 'HOLD POINT' witnessed by the Company's representative.

Question: During hot-tapping, a leak develops at the machine flange. What must the Worksite Supervisor ensure first?
A: Retrieve the cutter, close the valve and stop safely
B: Continue cutting at reduced speed to finish the bore
C: Tighten the flange bolts while the machine is running
D: Have the fire watch spray the flange and continue
Reference: Cl. 4.4: if any hazardous situation (e.g. leak) is observed, ensure the cutter is retrieved, the isolation valve closed and hot work stopped safely.

Question: Under which type of work permit must hot-tapping be carried out?
Reference: Cl. 5.1: in-service welding, hot-tapping and plugging must be under the control of a Hot Work Permit.

Question: What is 'hot-tapping' as defined in KOC.SA.019?
A: Cutting into live equipment via a fitting
B: Welding a patch on a depressurized line
C: Cutting threads into a cold pipe end
D: Heating a pipe to free a seized valve
Reference: Cl. 2.3: creating an opening on in-service equipment by cutting or drilling within an attached fitting using a hot-tap machine.

Question: When endorsing a permit for in-service welding, what must the Inspection Engineer record?
A: Expected duration of the welding job
B: Number of fire extinguishers at site
C: Welder's name and KOC ID number
D: Wall thickness, MAOP and flow limits
Reference: Cl. 4.2: mention minimum metal thickness obtained, maximum allowable operating pressure and flow requirements permitted during welding.

Question: Under what weather conditions is hot-tapping NOT carried out unless approved by KOC with an enclosure?
D: High wind, storm, dust or rain
Reference: Cl. 5.3.1 i: hot-tapping shall not be carried out during high windy, stormy, dusty and wet conditions unless approved with a covered enclosure.

Question: What fire watch arrangement does KOC.SA.019 require during hot-tapping?
A: None if the gas test reads 0% LEL
C: A fire watch during night work only
D: The welder watches for fire himself
Reference: Cl. 5.3.1 xvi: a dedicated fire watch shall be established and equipped with a suitable extinguisher or pressurized fire hose.

Question: What gas monitoring must be specified in the work permit for hot-tapping?
A: Monitoring only if a leak is suspected
C: One test at the start of the shift
Reference: Cl. 4.3: gas test before commencement; continuous gas monitoring shall be specified in the work permit.

Question: Which communication must be available between the Worksite Supervisor and Operations during hot-tapping?
C: Two-way radio to the control room
D: Hand signals from the work site
Reference: Cl. 4.4: two-way radio communication shall be made available between Worksite Supervisor and Operations in the control room.

Question: When may the hot-tapping machine be removed after completing the tap?
A: At the end of the working shift, as normal
B: After the checklist is completed and agreed
C: Immediately after the cutting is finished
D: As soon as the fire watch has left the site
Reference: Cl. 5.4: the machine shall not be removed until the required checklist is completely filled and agreed by KOC concerned teams.

Question: Hot-tapping is to be done in an underground access pit. Which additional procedure applies?
Reference: Cl. 5.3.1 xi: KOC.SA.007 shall be followed; personnel should be equipped with a retrieval system.

Question: How must the operating pressure and temperature of the line compare with the hot-tapping machine rating?
A: Only pressure must be within rating
B: They must never exceed its ratings
C: They may exceed it if cutting is slow
D: They may exceed its ratings by 10%
Reference: Cl. 5.3.2: operating pressure and temperature shall at no time exceed the rated pressure and temperature of the cutting machine.

Question: When line packers, seal plugs or expandable plugs are used, which procedure governs the mechanical isolation?
D: KOC.SA.035 Safe Use of Gas Cylinders
Reference: Cl. 4.3 / 5.3.3: mechanical isolation shall be carried out as per KOC.PS.016 when using line packers / seal plugs.

Question: Who may carry out hot-tapping work in KOC?
A: KOC-approved contractor or KOC specialist crew
B: Any welder who holds a valid Hot Work Permit
C: Operators from the Permit Issuer's own team
D: Any mechanical contractor working on the site
Reference: Cl. 4.5: hot-tapping shall be carried out by the KOC approved contractor or the KOC specialized maintenance crew.

Question: While welding is in progress, within what radius of the work must the assigned Fire Watch remain until relieved?
Reference: Cl. 4.5: the Fire Watch shall remain within 8 m radius of the work vicinity during welding / cutting until relieved.

Question: After a welding job is completed, how long must the Fire Watch remain at the location?
Reference: Cl. 4.5: remain at least 30 minutes after hot work until the area is inspected and found free of ignition sources.

Question: Before welding in a plant area, flammable materials must be cleared, and drains covered with wet tarpaulins, within what distance of the worksite?
Reference: Cl. 5.7: flammable materials cleared at least 20 m away; all drains within 20 m covered with wet tarpaulins weighted with sandbags.

Question: Under KOC.SA.021, acetylene must not be generated, piped or used at a pressure exceeding:
Reference: Cl. 5.4: under no condition shall acetylene be used at a pressure in excess of 15 psig (103 kPa gauge).

Question: Why must fittings containing more than 70% copper (other than a burner tip) not be used in acetylene welding equipment?
A: Copper corrodes rapidly in contact with oxygen
B: Copper and acetylene form explosive copper acetylide
C: Copper conducts heat back and causes flashback
D: Copper lowers the flame temperature too much
Reference: Cl. 5.2: copper in contact with acetylene is liable to form a dangerous explosive compound, copper acetylide.

Question: Which filter lens shade range does KOC.SA.021 specify for electric arc welding?
Reference: Cl. 5.3 Lens Shade Guide: arc welding 10–14; torch brazing 3–4; gas welding 4–8; cutting 3–6.

Question: What minimum distance must an electric arc welding generator be kept from the hot work area?
Reference: Cl. 5.5: the welding generator should be kept at least 5 m away from the hot work area.

Question: A pipe must be cold cut inside a hazardous area. Which equipment is permitted under KOC.SA.021?
B: Pneumatic cold cutting machine or manual cutter
C: Abrasive disc cutter with a spark guard
D: Any cutter, provided a fire watch is present
Reference: Cl. 5.6: in a hazardous area only pneumatic cold cutting machines and manual cutters are allowed; electric-driven cutting machines are not allowed.

Question: Which coverall is mandatory for all welding and cutting jobs under KOC.SA.021?
Reference: Cl. 5.3: Inherently Flame Resistant (IFR) coverall with suitable aprons, sleeves and leggings is mandatory for all welding and cutting jobs.

Question: What must welders NOT wear while welding?
B: Helmet with an auto-dark filter lens
Reference: Cl. 5.2: welders should not wear metallic jewelry, rings, or watchstraps.

Question: What is the explosive range of acetylene in air stated in KOC.SA.021?
Reference: Cl. 5.4 / 5.7: explosions are possible from 2% by volume up to 82% acetylene in air.

Question: Under KOC.SA.021, the deployment of welding equipment mounted on mobile trucks is:
C: Allowed with a Vehicle Entry Permit
D: Allowed if the engine is stopped
Reference: Cl. 5.4: the deployment of welding equipment mounted on mobile trucks is prohibited in all areas.

Question: An arc welding generator should have an automatic voltage regulator to reduce the open-circuit voltage to a safe limit, normally about:
Reference: Cl. 5.5: the arc welding generator should include an automatic voltage regulator reducing open circuit voltage to a safe limit, normally 15 volts.

Question: A welding cable is too short. How may two lengths be joined?
A: With a splice wrapped in insulating tape
B: With standard plug and socket couplers
C: By twisting the bare cores together
D: With a screw-type jubilee hose clip
Reference: Cl. 5.5: if joints are necessary, standard plug and socket couplings shall be used; splices are not allowed in welding cables.

Question: Where should an electrode holder be placed when not in use?
A: On a wooden rest, not on the ground
B: On the ground beside the welder
C: On the steel structure being welded
D: Hanging by its cable from the work piece
Reference: Cl. 5.5: the electrode holder should not be placed on the ground; wooden rests should be provided.

Question: Where must an arc strike or test be carried out?
Reference: Cl. 5.5: in no case shall an arc strike / test be conducted on the equipment or structure; it shall be conducted on test plates.

Question: When may an engine-driven welding machine be refuelled?
B: While running, if the welder stops welding
C: Any time, if a fire extinguisher is nearby
D: Only when it is not in operation
Reference: Cl. 5.5: any engine driven welding machine shall not be refuelled while in operation.

Question: Under KOC.SA.021, what can a gas plug be relied on for when preparing a pipe for welding?
Reference: Cl. 5.1: a gas plug will not be considered positive isolation for retaining liquid or pressure, but can be used for sealing off vapours only.

Question: Welding is to be done 3 m above ground. What access does KOC.SA.021 require?
A: A stepladder held by a helper
D: A ladder lashed to the pipe
Reference: Cl. 5.2: where welding is above 1.8 m, proper scaffolding shall be provided per the Working at Height Procedure.

Question: Before cutting the bottom of a tank, what must be done?
A: Cut a small pilot hole with a torch
B: Paint the cut line with primer
C: Drill test holes and gas test below
D: Flood the tank up to the cut level
Reference: Cl. 5.2: before cutting the bottom of any tank, test holes must be drilled and gas tests carried out.

Question: How should ventilation be provided when welding inside a confined space?
B: Natural ventilation through the manway only
C: Opening an oxygen cylinder valve inside
D: Blowing compressed oxygen into the space
Reference: Cl. 5.8: ventilation by extraction fans or air movers rather than blowing fresh air in; compressed oxygen shall never be used.

Question: Under the KOC multi-lock sequence for electrical isolation, who applies the FIRST lock?
A: The Permit Issuer, before issuing the permit
B: The Authorized Electrical Person, after confirming isolation
C: The Worksite Supervisor, after receiving the permit
D: The Shift Controller, after approving the request
Reference: Cl. 5.6 (i): the first lock shall be applied by the Authorized Electrical Person immediately after confirming electrical isolation.

Question: On completion of work, what is the correct order for removing locks from the multi-lock device before electrical de-isolation?
A: Electrical Person, then Permit Issuer, then Worksite Supervisor
B: Permit Issuer, then Worksite Supervisor, then Electrical Person
C: Worksite Supervisor, then Permit Issuer, then Electrical Person
D: Shift Controller removes all locks together at one time
Reference: Cl. 5.6: the sequence is reversed for removal — Worksite Supervisor / Permit Applicant first, Permit Issuer second, Authorized Electrical Person last.

Question: Which of the following is NOT considered an energy isolating device under KOC.SA.022?
D: A cut-out fuse on the supply circuit
Reference: Cl. 2.0: push buttons, selector switches and other control circuit type devices are not energy isolating devices.

Question: Why does KOC.SA.022 state that Miniature Circuit Breakers (MCBs) should not be used as the point of disconnection?
A: They trip too easily under normal load
B: Positive contact separation cannot be confirmed
C: They cannot be fitted with any warning tag
D: They are only rated for very low voltages
Reference: Cl. 5.1 f): do not use MCBs as disconnections because confirming positive contact separation is generally not possible.

Question: For multi-disciplinary jobs, KOC.SA.022 recommends colour-coded padlocks. Which colour is assigned to Operations?
Reference: Cl. 5.6: Yellow – Electrical / Blue – Operation / Black – Mechanical / Red – Instrument.

Question: What is the minimum number of individually marked key storage boxes each facility must have for multi-lockout keys?
Reference: Cl. 5.7: each facility shall have at least 4 key storage boxes (Electrical, Mechanical, Instrumentation & Operation).

Question: An urgent electrical isolation is needed to protect the plant and workforce. Under KOC.SA.022, how may it be authorized?
A: Verbally by the Authorized Electrical Person or Shift Controller
B: Only after a written Electrical Isolation Certificate is approved
C: Verbally by any Worksite Supervisor who is present at site
D: Only by the Asset HSE Team after carrying out a site visit
Reference: Cl. 5.4: emergency isolation can be carried out immediately by verbal approval of the Authorized Electrical Person or Shift Controller; written formalities completed once the emergency is over.

Question: After isolating and locking an electrical motor, how must the absence of voltage be confirmed before work starts?
A: By pressing the local start button to check it does not run
B: By testing with an appropriate and tested voltage tester
C: By checking the breaker indicator light is off
D: By confirming with the Control Room Operator by radio
Reference: Cl. 4.4 / 5.1 j)–k): verify isolation by electrical measurement; presence of voltage must be tested using an appropriate and tested voltage tester.

Question: In the multi-lock sequence, who applies the SECOND lock?
B: Permit Issuer, before issuing the permit
Reference: Cl. 5.6 (ii): the 2nd lock shall be applied by the Asset Owner (Permit Issuer) prior to issuance of the Work Permit.

Question: Who applies the THIRD lock on the multi-lock device?
A: Shift Controller, at the next shift change
C: Worksite Supervisor, after receiving the permit
D: Permit Issuer, just before issuing the permit
Reference: Cl. 5.6 (iii): the 3rd lock shall be applied by the Worksite Supervisor or Permit Applicant after receiving the work permit.

Question: In the recommended KOC colour coding, which discipline uses a BLACK padlock?
Reference: Cl. 5.6: Yellow – Electrical / Blue – Operation / Black – Mechanical / Red – Instrument.

Question: Who authorizes an Authorized Electrical Person in writing?
A: Asset HSE Team Leader of the area
D: Permit Issuer of the operating area
Reference: Cl. 2.0: an Authorized Electrical Person is authorized in writing by the respective area Snr. Engineer Electrical.

Question: Which instruction is typical on an electrical tag-out sign?
Reference: Cl. 5.1 / 5.2: tags convey clear instructions such as 'Do Not Start', 'Do Not Energize' or 'Do Not Operate'.

Question: How long must the Electrical Isolation / De-isolation Logbook be retained?
Reference: Cl. 8.0: Electrical Isolation / De-isolation Logbook — 5 years.

Question: During isolation, what must be done about stored electrical energy in batteries and capacitors?
B: Leave it, as it is harmless
Reference: Cl. 5.1 g): release or render safe all stored or residual energy; stored energy discharged, taking care with batteries and capacitors.

Question: What marking must a LOTO padlock carry so it can be recorded on the Isolation Certificate?
Reference: Cl. 5.2 e): padlock should have a duly imprinted number for record in the Isolation Certificate.

Question: According to KOC.SA.022, a 'Danger Notice' indicates a hazard that if not avoided could result in:
Reference: Cl. 2.0: Danger Notice — could result in death or serious injury; Caution Notice — minor or moderate injury.

Question: At a project site outside KOC facilities, who approves a contractor's electrical isolation request after review by the contractor's electrical engineer?
Reference: Cl. 4.3 / 5.1: request reviewed by contractor electrical engineer / supervisor and approved by the KOC representative at site.

Question: Before an isolated machine is re-energized, what must be done first?
C: Ask the operator to start it locally
D: Switch on and watch for sparks
Reference: Cl. 5.3: clear tools and materials from the machine and clear employees from the area before removing locks and energizing.

Question: Under what condition may the Control Room Operator (Operator-I) request an electrical isolation for operational need?
B: At any time, without any approval
D: Only during the day shift hours
Reference: Cl. 4.5–4.6: Operator-I can request isolation only with due approval from the Shift Controller; recorded in the Operator-I logbook.

Question: According to the KOC.SA.024 JSA flow, who initiates, reviews and authorizes a JSA, respectively?
A: Permit Applicant, Permit Issuer, HSE Team
B: Worksite Supervisor, Permit Applicant, Permit Issuer
C: Safety Officer, Worksite Supervisor, Permit Applicant
D: Permit Issuer, Permit Applicant, Worksite Supervisor
Reference: Cl. 5.9 / Appendix 1: JSA initiated by Worksite Supervisor, reviewed by Permit Applicant, authorized by Permit Issuer.

Question: For which activities does KOC.SA.024 require a JSA WITH Task Risk Assessment (initial and residual risk)?
Reference: Cl. 2.0 / 5.4: JSA with Task Risk Assessment will be carried out only for critical activities.

Question: A contractor submits a JSA copied from a similar job at another gathering centre. Under the 2025 revision of KOC.SA.024, this is:
A: Acceptable if the Permit Issuer signs it
C: Prohibited; a task-specific JSA is needed
D: Acceptable if reviewed at the toolbox talk
Reference: Cl. 5.1 Note: the use of generic JSA is strictly prohibited; a standalone JSA specific to the exact task, location and worksite conditions must be developed.

Question: In KOC.SA.024, 'residual risk' is best defined as the risk:
A: Present before any controls are applied
B: Remaining after controls have been applied
C: Linked to the worst credible outcome only
D: Accepted by the Permit Issuer without controls
Reference: Cl. 2.0: residual risk is the risk remaining after controls have been applied to associated hazards that have been identified.

Question: What size of Risk Assessment Matrix (Severity vs Likelihood) is used in the current KOC JSA template?
Reference: Revision 3 Aug 2025 / Appendix 1: RAM changed to 6x6 Severity vs Likelihood to align with KOC.GE.018.

Question: When a JSA is prepared for a job that involves the use of chemicals, what should it include?
A: A review of the Safety Data Sheets (SDS)
D: A medical surveillance record for each worker
Reference: Cl. 5.5: JSAs for jobs that involve the use of chemicals should include a review of SDS sheets.

Question: On completion of a job carried out under a work permit, where is the JSA sheet retained as a record?
B: With the Permit Issuer, in file
D: It is discarded once the permit is closed
Reference: Cl. 5.7: on completion, the JSA sheet shall be retained in file with the Permit Issuer (routine work without permit: with the Controlling Team).

Question: A Task Risk Assessment shows the residual risk remains in the intolerable region and engineering alternatives are not feasible. Under the KOC JSA risk regime, the activity may proceed only:
A: With Manager-level endorsement and a risk-reduction action plan
B: If the Worksite Supervisor holds an extra toolbox talk on it
C: If the Permit Issuer marks the permit as a critical activity
D: If additional PPE is issued to every worker on the task
Reference: Appendix 1 Risk Control Regime: intolerable risk — activity shall only proceed upon KOC Management endorsement (Manager and above) supported by a detailed action plan.

Question: What does a Job Safety Analysis (JSA) do?
A: Records attendance at a toolbox talk
B: Lists the tools and materials for a job
C: Calculates the cost and duration of a job
D: Breaks a job into steps and controls hazards
Reference: Cl. 2.0: JSA analyzes each job by breaking it into steps, identifying hazards, assessing risk and recommending precautions; also called Job Hazard Analysis.

Question: During work under a permit, where must the JSA sheet be kept?
B: At site, with the work permit copy
Reference: Cl. 4.3 / 5.7: the JSA sheet is kept / attached with the work permit copy at site.

Question: How should the Worksite Supervisor brief workers on the JSA before starting work?
A: By e-mail to the whole crew the day before
B: By giving a copy to the crew foreman only
C: Through the daily toolbox talk or pre-job meeting
D: By posting a copy on the camp notice board
Reference: Cl. 4.3: brief JSA to workers through daily Toolbox Talks / Pre-Job Meeting and ensure all are familiar with it.

Question: Which job should be given priority for a JSA under KOC.SA.024?
A: A routine task with no incident history
B: A task covered by an approved SOP
D: A new job not done before
Reference: Cl. 5.1: priority includes new jobs, modified jobs, infrequently performed jobs, potential for severe injury and incident history.

Question: How is the Task Risk Assessment carried out for a critical activity?
A: Assessed before and again after controls
C: Assessed only by the Asset HSE Team
D: Assessed only for the riskiest step
Reference: Cl. 5.4: TRA considers initial and residual risks in two steps — before and after application of control measures.

Question: Which group conducts periodic audits of JSA procedure compliance in each directorate?
Reference: Cl. 4.5: the corporate HSE Group is responsible to conduct periodical audit verifying compliance with the JSA Procedure.

Question: Which event requires an existing JSA to be modified?
A: Each time a new worker joins the crew
B: Only after an HSE audit finds a gap
C: A change in procedure, equipment or process
D: Only once a year on a fixed review date
Reference: Cl. 5.8: in case of procedural change, equipment upgrade, change in job or process, JSA will be modified.

Question: At shift change, what must the Permit Issuer do with the JSA before endorsing the permit?
B: Nothing; JSA review is only at issue
C: Send it to the HSE Group
D: Discard it and issue a new one
Reference: Cl. 4.2: the Permit Issuer will also review JSA prior to endorsing the permit on shift change.

Question: In KOC.SA.024, 'likelihood' is defined as:
A: The cost of controls for the hazard
B: The degree of harm if it occurs
C: The expected probability of an event
Reference: Cl. 2.0: Likelihood — a measure of the expected probability or frequency of an event's occurrence.

Question: How is the risk rating obtained in a KOC Task Risk Assessment?
B: By the number of workers involved
C: By counting the number of hazards
D: By the length of the job
Reference: Cl. 2.0: the risk rating is calculated by comparing severity and likelihood of the event's occurrence.

Question: Which of the following is a KOC Life Saving Rule printed on the JSA template?
A: Attend the weekly site safety meeting
B: Obtain authorization before confined space entry
C: Carry your company ID card at all times
D: Always work in pairs during the night shift
