Reference: Appendix 1, Section A: Life Saving Rules include 'Obtain Authorization before entering a Confined Space'.

Question: When does the Asset / Directorate HSE Team take part in a Task Risk Assessment?
A: For every routine job without exception
B: Only after an incident has occurred
C: Never; TRA is for operations only
D: When the Controlling Team requests support
Reference: Cl. 4.4: ensure HSE Team participation in the Task Risk Assessment when support is requested from the Controlling Team.

Question: During excavation in an EOD-certified area, a worker uncovers a suspected unexploded shell. What is the correct sequence of first actions?
A: Lift it out carefully and carry it away from the trench
B: Leave it untouched, clear and mark the area, move away, call 160
C: Photograph it close up on a mobile phone and send it to HSE
D: Cover it with sand and carry on in another part of the trench
Reference: Cl. 5.2.4: do not touch; stop work and clear area; mark location at a safe distance; move away before using radio/phone; inform Fire Station / 160; request EOD assistance.

Question: Before electric shot firing with electric detonators, all radio communication equipment within what range must be switched off?
Reference: Cl. 5.1.3.3: handheld radios / transmitters not within 150 m; all radio equipment within 150 m switched off before electric shot firing.

Question: A charge fired by safety fuse has misfired. What is the minimum time before anyone may approach it?
Reference: Cl. 5.1.3.2: no one should approach until not less than 30 minutes (safety fuse) or 10 minutes (electric firing) has elapsed.

Question: Under KOC.SA.025, no naked flame, spark or source of ignition is permitted within what distance of an explosive storage facility?
Reference: Cl. 5.1.1.2: any naked flame, spark or source of ignition shall not be permitted within 25 m (80 ft) of the explosive storage facility.

Question: As a minimum, how far must a permanent explosive storage facility be located from any other building or place visited by employees or the public?
Reference: Cl. 5.1.1.1: permanent explosive storage must be at least 100 m from any other building, habitation or place liable to be visited.

Question: Which arrangement for transporting explosives and detonators to a well site complies with KOC.SA.025?
A: Both in the same vehicle, in separate compartments
B: Both in the same container, if detonators are shunted
C: In separate vehicles, with no explosives in the driver's cab
D: Detonators in the driver's cab, explosives in the cargo bed
Reference: Cl. 5.1.2: explosives and detonators must be transported separately and not in the same vehicle; no explosive in the driver's cab.

Question: What is the maximum number of charges that should be prepared and loaded for any single firing operation?
Reference: Cl. 5.1.3.1: a maximum of ten charges should be prepared and loaded for any single firing operation; count the shots fired.

Question: A Controlling Team wants to start work in a new desert area. Which form of EOD clearance is acceptable under KOC.SA.025?
A: Verbal confirmation from the EOD contractor's supervisor
B: A printed EOD certificate with the cleared area marked on a map
C: An e-mail from any HSE Officer stating the area is clear
D: A note on the Permit to Work that the area appears clear
Reference: Cl. 5.2.3: EOD certification shall be issued on printed format with extent of clearance marked on a map; verbal clearance is not acceptable.

Question: An electrically fired charge has misfired. What is the minimum waiting time before anyone approaches it?
Reference: Cl. 5.1.3.2: not less than 10 minutes for firing by electricity (30 minutes for safety fuse).

Question: At what minimum distance from the explosive store building or containers must the security fence be located?
Reference: Cl. 5.1.1.1: explosive storage facility shall be enclosed by fencing at least 15 m from the building or containers.

Question: How far from the walls must the wooden shelves holding explosive boxes be placed?
Reference: Cl. 5.1.1.2: boxes stacked on wooden shelves placed at least 15 cm (6") away from walls for air circulation.

Question: Within what distance of a box of explosives is it prohibited to carry a lighter, matches or mobile phone?
Reference: Cl. 5.1.3.1: prohibited to carry lighter, matches, mobile phone or any ignition source within 30 m (100 ft) of explosives.

Question: Who may travel in a vehicle carrying explosives?
A: Any crew members going to the site
B: The driver and one trained attendant
C: The driver only, with no attendant
D: Up to four trained shot firers
Reference: Cl. 5.1.2.2: the driver shall be accompanied by one trained attendant; no extra person is permitted.

Question: When must a vehicle carrying explosives be refuelled?
B: When the tank falls below one quarter
C: Only on highways with police escort
D: At any fuel station on the way
Reference: Cl. 5.1.2.2: sufficient fuel before loading, as refuelling is not permitted during transportation.

Question: What hand lamps must a vehicle carrying explosives carry?
A: Two IS lamps, one red glass, one clear
B: No lamps; hazard lights are enough
C: Two LED lamps of any colour
D: One ordinary torch with spare batteries
Reference: Cl. 5.1.2.2: two battery operated intrinsically safe hand lamps, one fitted with red glass and the other clear.

Question: Detonators and high explosives with a mass explosion risk and minor missile effect belong to which category?
Reference: Cl. 2.0: Category ZZ — mass explosion risk and minor missile effect, e.g. high explosives, detonators, detonating fuse.

Question: How often must the Controlling Team inspect each explosive storage facility?
Reference: Cl. 4.3 / 5.1.1.4: inspect explosive storage facilities at least every three months.

Question: If tamping is needed after a cartridge is placed in a shot hole, what rod must be used?
A: A steel bar of suitable length
D: A wooden rod with no ferrous parts
Reference: Cl. 5.1.3.1: in case of tamping need, a wooden rod without any ferrous part is to be used.

Question: Unused or loose explosives returned to store should be consumed or disposed of within:
Reference: Cl. 5.1.4: unutilized or loose explosive materials should be consumed or disposed of within one week of return.

Question: How must detonator leads be kept while in storage?
B: Taped firmly to the explosive cartridges
C: Connected to the exploder unit in store
D: Shunted together until just before use
Reference: Cl. 5.1.1.3: detonator leads must be shunted together while stored and kept this way until right before use.

Question: What material must a portable container for carrying explosives be made of?
C: Any metal box with a tight lid
D: Mild steel box with a padlock
Reference: Cl. 5.1.2.1: container and cover must be of non-ferrous material (leather, rubber, plastic, wood, canvas); fittings of brass.

Question: What is the minimum distance from a hydrocarbon-carrying pipeline within which mechanical excavation (including levelling with an excavator) is prohibited?
Reference: Cl. 5.4 b): no mechanical excavation closer than 5 m to any hydrocarbon carrying pipeline, even for levelling.

Question: Without a Management of Change and risk assessment, mechanical excavation should not take place closer than what distance to non-hydrocarbon pipelines, cables and services?
Reference: Cl. 5.4 c): no mechanical excavation closer than 3 m to non-hydrocarbon pipelines, cables and services; MOC and risk assessment if closer.

Question: In a trench deeper than 1 m, how must access ladders be provided under KOC.SA.026?
A: Projecting 0.5 m above the edge, every 15 m of travel
B: Projecting 1 m above the edge, every 7.5 m of lateral travel
C: Projecting 1 m above the edge, every 15 m of lateral travel
D: Projecting 1.5 m above the edge, at each end only
Reference: Cl. 5.4 i): ladder projecting minimum 1 m above the edge; ladders every 7.5 m (25 ft) of lateral travel, secured top and bottom.

Question: For an excavation up to 1.2 m deep, what is the minimum distance excavated material (spoil) must be placed from the edge?
Reference: Cl. 5.4 l): excavated material shall be placed not less than 1 m from the edge for depth up to 1.2 m, increased in proportion to depth.

Question: Heavy equipment, materials and excavating machinery must be kept at least how far from the excavation area?
Reference: Cl. 5.4 n): heavy equipment, material or excavating machinery shall be kept clear from the excavation area by at least 3 m.

Question: Which barricading arrangement around an open trench meets KOC.SA.026?
A: Barrier tape tied between steel rebars
B: Hard fixed barriers with reflective warning signs
C: Rope strung between rebars at each corner
D: Spoil heaped along the edge as a bund
Reference: Cl. 4.3 / 5.4 k): hard fixed barriers with reflective warning notices, signs and flashing lights; tapes and rebars shall not be used as barriers.

Question: An excavation in Type B soil will exceed 1 m in depth. Which shoring arrangement meets KOC.SA.026?
A: No shoring if the sides are sloped at 30°
B: Sheeting 450 mm above ground; boards ≤ 750 mm apart
C: Polling boards 2 m apart; braces 2 m apart
D: No shoring if the trench is under 2 m deep
Reference: Cl. 5.6.1.2 a): Type B over 1 m — shoring required; sheeting at least 450 mm above ground; polling boards ≤ 750 mm apart; horizontal braces ≤ 1 m apart.

Question: In addition to the Excavation Notification, which work permit is required for excavation using a mechanical excavator?
Reference: Cl. 5.3 e) / 5.6.2: a Hot Work Permit is required for excavation involving a mechanical excavator; a Cold Work Permit for manual excavation.

Question: In addition to the Excavation Notification, which permit is required for MANUAL excavation with hand tools?
Reference: Cl. 4.1 / 5.3 e): Cold Work Permit for manual excavation; Hot Work Permit for mechanical excavation.

Question: Which clearance must be obtained before any excavation work in a KOC area?
A: Fire Team training certificate for crew
B: Municipality building permit for the site
Reference: Cl. 5.4 a): no excavation work in KOC area shall be undertaken without ensuring EOD clearance for that location.

Question: Why must a shovel with a metal handle NOT be used for manual excavation?
A: It rusts quickly in damp soil
B: Electrocution if a live cable is struck
C: It damages the soil layers below
D: It is heavier to lift all day long
Reference: Cl. 5.4 w): shovel with metal handle shall not be used for manual excavation to prevent the risk of electrocution.

Question: In Type A (cohesive) soil, up to what depth is shoring usually NOT required?
Reference: Cl. 5.6.1.1 a): for Type A soil, shoring is not usually required provided the depth does not exceed 1 m.

Question: In Type A soil where space permits, to what angle may the sides be sloped to excavate deeper without shoring?
Reference: Cl. 5.6.1.1 b): if surface area permits, greater depth can be made by sloping the side down to an angle of 45°.

Question: What support is required for excavation in Type C soil, such as sand or soil with water seeping?
A: No support if under 2 m deep
Reference: Cl. 5.6.1.3: in Type C or poor soil, close sheeting or a continued series of polling boards shall be used.

Question: Under KOC.SA.026, a trench is a narrow excavation whose bottom width is NOT greater than:
Reference: Cl. 2.0: the width of a trench (measured at the bottom) is not greater than 15 ft (4.6 m).

Question: Why must equipment with internal combustion engines NOT be kept inside an excavation?
A: It raises the noise above 85 dB
B: It blocks the ladder access route
C: It may sink into the soft soil
D: Exhaust gases such as CO build up
Reference: Cl. 5.4 t): such equipment shall not be kept inside the excavation to prevent accumulation of CO and CO2.

Question: In what layer thickness should excavations be backfilled and rammed?
Reference: Cl. 5.6.5: excavations shall be backfilled in 150 mm layers and solidly rammed and tamped.

Question: Contaminated soil is found in a spoil heap. How may it be used?
A: Used for the top 150 mm layer only
B: Mixed 50/50 with clean soil for backfill
C: Not used; disposed of per KOC.EV.008
D: Used if covered with plastic sheeting
Reference: Cl. 5.6.5: no contaminated soil shall be used for backfilling; it shall be disposed of per KOC.EV.008.

Question: May a mechanical excavator dig while workers are inside the trench?
A: Yes, if a banksman is present
B: Yes, if they stay 2 m from the bucket
C: No, never while personnel are inside
D: Yes, for the final 0.5 m only
Reference: Cl. 5.6.2 e): mechanical excavation shall not be carried out while personnel are inside the trench / excavation.

Question: Excavation work may affect the bund wall of a crude oil storage tank. Who must additionally endorse the Excavation Notification?
Reference: Cl. 4.7 / 5.3 d): for bund wall cutting or excavation affecting the bunded area, the Excavation Notification shall be endorsed by the Fire Team.

Question: What must be done with the bucket of a loader or backhoe when it is not in operation?
A: Rest it on the spoil heap edge
Reference: Cl. 5.6.2 g): the bucket must always be lowered to the ground if the loader or backhoe is not in operation.

Question: How does KOC.SA.027 define 'High Voltage'?
C: A system voltage of 1000 V and above
D: A system voltage of 3300 V and above
Reference: Cl. 2.0: High Voltage – a system voltage of 3300 volts and above; Low Voltage – not exceeding 440 volts.

Question: Portable tools and extension cords above 50 V to ground that are frequently plugged and unplugged must be protected by an RCD with a maximum trip setting of:
Reference: Cl. 5.1: such equipment must be protected by permanent or portable RCDs with a 30 mA maximum current setting.

Question: A crane must pass under an existing 132 kV overhead power line. What is the minimum vertical clearance required between the lowest conductor and the top of the equipment?
Reference: Cl. 5.1 table: for 33 kV & 132 kV lines, minimum vertical safety clearance from lowest conductor to top of equipment is 5 m (10 m from ground).

Question: A portable hand lamp on a trailing lead is needed inside a confined space. What does KOC.SA.027 require?
A: Supply not exceeding 24 V and explosion-proof type
B: Supply not exceeding 110 V with an RCD
C: Supply not exceeding 240 V with double insulation
D: Any lamp, if the space is gas free
Reference: Cl. 5.2: for a portable hand lamp on a trailing lead inside a confined space, supply voltage shall not exceed 24 V and only explosion-proof type shall be used.

Question: When an isolated LV/HV conductor is earthed by installing a copper earthing conductor, what is its minimum cross-section?
Reference: Cl. 5.3 C: each conductor shall be earthed by fixed earthing switch, CB, or a copper conductor of minimum cross section 25 sq. mm.

Question: Before starting work inside a substation protected by a CO2 or clean-agent suppression system, what must the authorized electrical person do?
A: Disable the fire alarm panel for the whole shift
B: Switch the system to Manual/Maintenance mode
C: Open all doors so any released gas can escape
D: Keep the system on Auto and wear an SCBA set
Reference: Cl. 4.4 / 5.3 A: turn the system to Manual/Maintenance mode on entry and return it to Normal (Auto) mode after the job and evacuation; record in the logbook.

Question: A worker is unconscious and still in contact with an electrical source. What does KOC.SA.027 say should be done first?
A: Pull the victim away by the clothing
B: Free the victim using a Rescue Stick
C: Pour water on the equipment to trip it
Reference: Cl. 5.2: the victim should be removed safely from the electrical source by means of a Rescue Stick and artificial respiration given by trained personnel.

Question: Under the 'Test Before Touch' requirement of KOC.SA.027, how must the voltage tester itself be checked?
A: Only once a year when it is calibrated
B: On a known live source before and after use
C: Only before use, with its self-test button
D: Not needed when the tester is brand new
Reference: Cl. 5.1: Test Before Touch includes verifying test instruments on a known energized source before and after the test for absence of voltage.

Question: Before cutting an isolated high voltage cable, what must be done at the point of cut?
A: Wrap the cable with insulating tape
B: Spike it with a spiking gun or earthed spike
C: Test insulation resistance at 5 kV first
D: Hang a caution notice at the cut point
Reference: Cl. 5.3 D: HV cables shall be spiked at the point where they are to be cut by a spiking gun or a wooden-shafted, earthed steel-shod spike.

Question: How does KOC.SA.027 define 'Low Voltage'?
Reference: Cl. 2.0: Low Voltage — a system voltage not exceeding 440 volts.

Question: Until proven otherwise with a meter or tester, electrical equipment must be considered:
Reference: Cl. 2.0: all electrical equipment are considered to be energized until proven otherwise (using a meter / tester).

Question: Under KOC.SA.027, work on electrical circuitry must NOT be carried out by:
Reference: Cl. 5.2: any works on electrical circuitry should not be conducted by a single or lone person.

Question: Which plugs and sockets must be used at KOC locations other than offices and houses?
Reference: Cl. 4.3 / 5.2: only industrial type plugs and sockets shall be used on all locations other than offices and houses.

Question: What minimum vertical clearance is required between a 400 kV overhead line and the top of passing equipment?
Reference: Cl. 5.1 table: 400 kV — 7 m minimum vertical clearance from lowest conductor to top of equipment (12 m from ground).

Question: What minimum vertical clearance is required between a 3.3 kV overhead line and the top of passing equipment?
Reference: Cl. 5.1 table: 3.3 kV — 2 m clearance to top of equipment; 5 m clearance from ground.

Question: When a new asphalt road is built under an existing overhead line, what height barriers does KOC.SA.027 (MEW requirement) specify?
C: 7 m high, in each direction of traffic
D: 5 m high, in each direction of traffic
Reference: Cl. 5.1: height barriers of 5 m height shall be installed in each direction of traffic.

Question: A small fire starts on an electrical panel. What is the correct first action?
A: Isolate the supply, then use an extinguisher
B: Wait for the Fire Team without acting
C: Open the panel door to inspect the fire
D: Spray water on the panel straight away
Reference: Cl. 5.2: in the event of fire on electrical panel, the power supply must be isolated and a suitable extinguisher used.

Question: During work inside a substation, where must the authorized electrical person be?
A: In the substation for the whole job
C: In the control room, on the radio
D: At site only at start and finish
Reference: Cl. 5.3 A: the authorized electrical person shall remain present in the substation during the entire work period.

Question: Where work on a live LV cable is unavoidable, how many conductors may be bared at a time?
D: All, if insulated gloves are worn
Reference: Cl. 5.3 F: only one conductor should be bared at a time, with rubber boots, mats or gloves.

Question: Which type of ladder must NOT be used for electrical work or in substations?
Reference: Cl. 5.2: portable metal ladders / stepladders should not be used for electrical work or in substations.

Question: In an emergency, who may isolate a low or high voltage switch?
Reference: Cl. 5.3 B: in an emergency, anyone may isolate a LV / HV switch; such action must be immediately reported to the respective authority.

Question: After work on isolated HV apparatus is complete and earths are removed, what test should be carried out before re-energizing?
Reference: Cl. 5.3 C: remove earth connections and perform an Insulation Resistance test before voltage test or re-energizing; discharge equipment after the test.

Question: A single crane will lift a load equal to 80% of its rated capacity at the planned radius. Under KOC.SA.029, this lift is:
A: A standard lift, since it is below 100% of capacity
B: A critical lift, because it exceeds 75% of rated capacity
C: A critical lift only if it also exceeds 50 tonnes
D: A standard lift if it is done in daylight
Reference: Cl. 2.0 Critical lift: loads exceeding 75% of the rated capacity of any one crane.

Question: Which of the following lifts is classified as a critical lift by height under KOC.SA.029?
A: A lift exceeding 10 m in height
B: A lift exceeding 20 m in height
C: A lift exceeding 30 m in height
D: A lift exceeding 50 m in height
Reference: Cl. 2.0 Critical lift: lifts which exceed 30 m in height (also > 50 tonnes, > 75% capacity, multiple cranes, man-lifting, etc.).

Question: What is the minimum age for an operator of load handling equipment under KOC.SA.029?
Reference: Cl. 2.0 Operator: should be minimum 21 years of age, with 3rd party training certificates for the equipment.

Question: A lifting sling is inspected in November. According to the KOC.SA.029 quarterly colour code, which colour should it carry?
Reference: Cl. 5.2: Q1 Apr–Jun Green; Q2 Jul–Sep Yellow; Q3 Oct–Dec Blue; Q4 Jan–Mar White.

Question: Above what wind speed at the personnel platform must a man-lifting operation not begin, or be terminated if in progress?
Reference: Cl. 5.6.5: when wind speed exceeds 15 mph (24 km/h) at the personnel platform, man-lifting must not begin or must be terminated.

Question: What minimum size of outrigger pad does KOC.SA.029 recommend under each crane outrigger float?
A: Same size as the outrigger foot
B: At least twice the size of the outrigger foot
C: At least three times the size of the outrigger foot
D: At least five times the size of the outrigger foot
Reference: Cl. 5.6.3: outrigger pad size should be at least three times the size of the outrigger foot.

Question: When must a wire rope be removed from service due to broken wires under KOC.SA.029?
A: When any single broken wire is found
B: When broken wires exceed 10% in 8 diameters
C: When broken wires exceed 25% in one lay
D: Only when a full strand is broken
Reference: Cl. 5.8.3: wire rope shall not be used if, in any length of eight diameters, total visible broken wires exceed 10% of total wires.

Question: What is the maximum speed at which material handling equipment (e.g. a forklift) may be driven while operating inside a company facility?
Reference: Cl. 5.8.4: the equipment shall not be driven at a speed exceeding 8 km per hour while operating in a company facility.

Question: A contractor installs a fixed tower crane at a KOC site. What is the maximum validity of the Controlling Team's approval before the approval process must be repeated?
Reference: Cl. 5.3: approval for contractor fixed / permanently installed load handling equipment shall not exceed 12 months.

Question: A planned lift weighs 60 tonnes using one crane well within its capacity. How is it classified?
A: Standard lift, as it is within capacity
C: Critical lift, because it exceeds 50 tonnes
D: Standard lift if done in daylight
Reference: Cl. 2.0 Critical lift: lifts that exceed 50 tonnes in weight.

Question: How many banksmen should the crane operator take signals from at any time?
A: Whoever is closest to the cab
Reference: Cl. 5.6.3: the operator shall respond only to signals from one banksman who shall be clearly identified.

Question: How should a suspended load be controlled to prevent swinging?
A: By a worker holding the load by hand
Reference: Cl. 5.6.3: the load should be controlled using two guide ropes (tag lines) of adequate strength.

Question: What is the typical maximum in-service wind speed for mobile cranes given in KOC.SA.029?
Reference: Cl. 5.6.5: typical maximum in-service wind speed is 35 km/h for mobile cranes and 72 km/h for tower cranes.

Question: What minimum passageway must be kept between the slewing parts of a crane and nearby guardrails or fixtures?
Reference: Cl. 5.6.3: a passageway of minimum 610 mm shall be maintained between slewing / moving parts and guardrails / fixtures.

Question: Is anyone allowed to ride on a load or hook suspended from a crane?
C: Yes, for short lifts under 2 m
Reference: Cl. 5.6.3: it is strictly prohibited for anybody to ride on loads, buckets or hooks suspended from a crane.

Question: Who carries out the daily inspection of a crane at the start of each shift?
Reference: Cl. 4.6 / 5.9.1: daily and weekly inspection shall be carried out by the load handling equipment operator.

Question: For how long must records of daily crane inspections be kept?
Reference: Cl. 5.9.2: daily inspection records maintained for 15 days (weekly inspection records for 30 days).

Question: What is the minimum number of full tucks in an eye splice made in a wire rope?
Reference: Cl. 5.8.3: an eye splice made in any wire rope shall have not less than three full tucks.

Question: A sling is slightly too long. How may it be shortened?
A: Tie a single knot in one leg
B: Clamp the extra length with a bolt
C: Do not shorten it with knots or loops
D: Wrap it twice around the hook
Reference: Cl. 5.8.2: sling shall not be shortened with knots, bolts or other makeshift devices or by looping around a crane hook.

Question: Why does KOC.SA.029 say wet webbing slings should not be used?
A: They become too heavy to handle
B: They cannot then be colour coded
Reference: Cl. 5.8.2: do not use wet webbing slings since it will reduce the sling rated capacity.

Question: What should be done when a load is first lifted?
A: Lift just clear, stop and check
C: Lift with people steadying it below
D: Swing it straight to the landing
Reference: Cl. 5.6.3: the load shall initially be lifted just clear of the supporting surface and brought to rest while slings and balance are checked.

Question: May lifting equipment be used to drag a load along the ground?
B: Yes, with a tag line attached
C: Yes, if the hoist rope stays vertical
Reference: Cl. 5.6.3: lifting equipment shall not be used for dragging load.

Question: Unless conditions warrant greater clearance, painting should not be carried out within what distance of potential ignition sources such as welding or flame cutting?
Reference: Cl. 5.10: no painting should be carried out within 75 feet of potential ignition sources.

Question: Which surface preparation method is prohibited under KOC.SA.030?
Reference: Cl. 5.4: sand blasting is prohibited.

Question: Which of the following must NOT be used for solvent cleaning of surfaces before painting?
B: Alkali cleaners from an approved supplier
Reference: Cl. 5.4: benzene, gasoline, carbon tetrachloride and chlorinated hydrocarbons with low TLVs (< 20 ppm) shall not be used for solvent cleaning.

Question: If practical alternatives exist, solvents and paints shall not be applied to surfaces warmer than:
Reference: Cl. 5.10: solvents and paints shall not be applied to surfaces warmer than 80°C if practical alternatives exist (and not flushed into containers hotter than 50°C).

Question: A painter suffers a small skin puncture from high-pressure fluid from an airless spray gun. What does KOC.SA.030 require?
A: Clean with solvent and apply a plaster
B: Continue work and report at the end of shift
D: Wash with soap and monitor for 24 hours
Reference: Cl. 5.5: emergency medical care shall be obtained immediately if any high pressure fluid penetrates the skin; injection injuries can be extremely serious.

Question: Inside a confined space, during which activities must all personnel wear respirable air-fed hoods under KOC.SA.030?
A: Only during abrasive blasting of surfaces
B: Only during airless spray painting work
C: During blasting, spraying, solvent or brush work
D: Only when the LEL reading exceeds 10%
Reference: Cl. 5.8: air-fed hoods shall be worn inside confined spaces whenever blasting or spray painting, solvent cleaning or brush painting is in progress.

Question: Where should paint or thinner be decanted from one container to another?
A: Inside the store, near the shelves
B: In the open air, away from hazardous operations
C: Inside the spray booth, exhaust running
D: At the work face, beside the item painted
Reference: Cl. 5.11: dispensing or decanting shall not take place within the store but in the open air away from areas of hazardous operations.

Question: What must be done whenever an airless spray gun is left unattended?
C: Point the gun into the paint bucket
Reference: Cl. 5.5: the trigger safety catch shall be engaged whenever the airless gun is left unattended; tip guard always in place while spraying.

Question: Where practicable, from which side of the object should spray painting be done?
Reference: Cl. 5.5: spray painting should be conducted from the upwind side of the object being coated, wherever practicable.

Question: Where may food be eaten under KOC.SA.030?
A: Not where paint is stored, handled or used
B: At the work face during breaks
C: In the paint store if the lids are closed
D: In the spray booth after spraying
Reference: Cl. 5.7: food shall not be brought into or consumed on premises where paint is stored, handled or used.

Question: A painter has paint on his hands. How should he clean his skin?
A: With the cleaning solvent used for spray guns
C: With thinner from the paint store
D: With special skin cleansers, not solvents
Reference: Cl. 5.7: solvents shall not be used for cleansing the skin; special skin cleansers shall be provided.

Question: Solvents shall not be flushed into containers hotter than:
Reference: Cl. 5.10: solvents shall not be flushed into containers that are hotter than 50°C.

Question: What must be done with switches, panel boards and motors in the area before spray painting?
Reference: Cl. 5.10: all electrical equipment such as switches, panel boards and motors must be de-energized before spray painting.

Question: While painting is in progress inside a confined space, hot work inside the same space is:
Reference: Cl. 5.9: hot work shall not be permitted inside the confined space during painting works.

Question: What is the minimum number of persons that should work together when painting inside a confined space?
Reference: Cl. 5.9: there should be minimum two persons to work in confined spaces.

Question: When should gas testing be carried out for painting work under KOC.SA.030?
A: Only if a smell is noticed
C: Only at the end of the shift
Reference: Cl. 5.1: gas test should be carried out per KOC.HE.003 before and after painting works.

Question: What safety device must be provided at the nozzle end of an abrasive blasting hose?
A: Flashback arrestor at the blast pot
B: Spark guard fitted on the nozzle tip
D: Pressure gauge fitted at the nozzle
Reference: Cl. 5.6: a dead man control device shall be provided at the nozzle end of the blasting hose.

Question: May extension cords or plug-in cords be used inside a spray paint booth?
A: Yes, if taped at the joints
B: No, they should not be used
Reference: Cl. 5.10: extension cords or other electrical plug-in cords should not be used in a spray paint booth.

Question: How often must the fit test of a painter's respirator be repeated?
Reference: Cl. 5.8 a): ensure the respirator is fit tested first and thereafter repeated at least annually.

Question: What must be marked on containers of lead-based paint?
D: The painter's name and KOC ID
Reference: Cl. 5.11: receptacles containing lead based paint must be legibly marked to alert about lead hazard.

Question: Under KOC.SA.031, an activity is defined as 'work at height' when it is carried out at an elevated location higher than:
Reference: Cl. 2.0: work at height is an activity at an elevated location of more than 1.8 m (6 ft) from the working ground level.

Question: What minimum load must a fixed anchor point be capable of supporting for each person attached to it?
Reference: Cl. 2.0 / 5.2.3.3: an anchorage must be capable of supporting at least 5,000 lb (22.2 kN) for each person attached.

Question: Which lanyard specification complies with KOC.SA.031 for use with a full body harness?
A: Max 1.8 m, shock absorber, self-locking hooks
C: Max 3 m, made of polypropylene rope
D: Any length, shortened by tying knots
Reference: Cl. 5.2.3.2: maximum lanyard length 1.8 m (6 ft), self-locking hooks each end, shock absorber; never shortened with knots; no polypropylene.

Question: As a general guideline, at what length of climb on a fixed ladder must appropriate fall protection be provided?
Reference: Cl. 5.2.2: appropriate fall protection must be provided whenever the length of climb on a fixed ladder equals or exceeds 24 ft (7.3 m).

Question: Which guardrail arrangement meets the KOC.SA.031 edge protection requirements?
A: Top rail 750 mm high; no mid rail needed
B: Top rail ≥ 950 mm; no gap over 470 mm
C: Top rail 1,200 mm; gaps up to 600 mm
D: Steel banding as top rail at 1,000 mm
Reference: Cl. 5.2.1 / 5.2.3.8: main guard rail at least 950 mm (normally 1,000 mm); no gap more than 470 mm; steel/plastic banding not permitted as rails.

Question: Which statement about personal fall arrest equipment is correct under KOC.SA.031?
A: A body belt may be used if it has a shock absorber
B: Body belts are prohibited; harness with 100% tie-off
C: 100% tie-off is needed only above 6 m in height
D: One lanyard is enough when moving between anchors
Reference: Cl. 5.2.3.1: full body harness with two shock-absorbing lanyards; use of a body belt for fall arrest is prohibited; ensure 100% tie-off.

Question: In addition to the user's visual pre-use check, how often must the Controlling Team ensure harnesses, lanyards and lifelines are formally inspected and tagged?
Reference: Cl. 5.3: all fall-arresting equipment shall be subjected to a monthly inspection program and tagged if fit for use.

Question: A worker's lanyard arrested a short fall, and the shock absorber appears undamaged. What does KOC.SA.031 require?
A: Re-use it after a careful visual check
B: Re-use it after re-packing the absorber
D: Use it for work restraint only
Reference: Cl. 5.2.3.2 / 5.3: components subjected to impact loading shall be removed from service; equipment involved in a fall must not be used again.

Question: Use of a crane-suspended man basket to lift workers is permitted only in exceptional cases. How must the lift be classified and planned?
A: As a standard lift with a JSA only
B: As a critical lift with a Critical Lift Plan
C: As routine work not requiring a permit
D: As a standard lift if fitted with guardrails
Reference: Cl. 5.2.2: use of a man basket shall be considered a critical lift; a Critical Lift Plan shall be prepared per KOC.SA.029.

Question: According to the work-at-height hierarchy of controls, what is the FIRST approach?
Reference: Cl. 5.1: fall elimination first, then fall prevention, then fall arresting as the last line of defence.

Question: What must a worker do with his safety helmet while climbing a ladder or working at height?
Reference: Cl. 5.2.2: the worker must wear the chin strap of the safety helmet to prevent its fall from the head.

Question: At what interval of vertical climb must an appropriate landing place be provided?
Reference: Cl. 5.2.2: a landing place of adequate size and strength shall be provided at every 30 ft (9 m) of vertical climb.

Question: How many persons may use a single vertical lifeline at the same time?
Reference: Cl. 5.2.3.4: a vertical lifeline shall be used by only one person at a time.

Question: What minimum breaking strength must a vertical lifeline (drop line) have?
Reference: Cl. 2.0: drop line must have a minimum breaking strength of 5,400 lb or 2,450 kg (OSHA 1926.104).

Question: Where should an anchor point for a lanyard be positioned?
Reference: Cl. 5.2.3.3: anchoring point always shall be above shoulder level.

Question: How often must safety nets be inspected for wear, damage and deterioration?
Reference: Cl. 5.2.3.7: safety nets shall be inspected at least once a week.

Question: How often must a standalone guardrail (not part of a scaffold) be inspected and tagged?
A: Before first use, then every 7 days
C: Every 3 months, by a third party
Reference: Cl. 5.2.3.8: standalone guardrails inspected before first use and every seven (7) days; a tag affixed.

Question: A guardrail top rail must withstand a force applied outward or downward of at least:
Reference: Cl. 5.2.3.8: guardrail system must withstand at least 200 lb (about 890 N) applied within 2 inches of the top edge.

Question: Two crews plan to work at height at different levels directly above one another. Under KOC.SA.031 this is:
B: Not allowed, due to falling objects
C: Allowed if both crews wear helmets
D: Allowed if upper crew uses tool lanyards
Reference: Cl. 5.2.1: simultaneous work at height shall not be allowed at multiple levels to avoid 'struck by falling object'.

Question: What is the minimum age for a person working on a suspended working platform (gondola)?
Reference: Cl. 5.2.2 b): every person on the working platform should be at least 18 years old, fit, agile and not suffer from acrophobia.

Question: Which material must NOT be used for lanyards and lifelines?
Reference: Cl. 5.2.3.2: manila, other natural fibres and polypropylene must not be used; nylon, Dacron, webbing or aircraft cable may be used.

Question: What is the minimum rope diameter for use with a rope grab under KOC.SA.031?
Reference: Cl. 5.2.3.5: the minimum diameter for rope grab shall be 1.59 cm (5/8 inch rope).

Question: In a cylinder store, oxygen cylinders must be separated from fuel-gas cylinders by a minimum of:
A: 3 m, or a 1 m high barrier
B: 6.1 m, or a 1.5 m high fire-rated barrier
C: 10 m, with no barrier option allowed
D: 15 m, or any solid wall of any height
Reference: Cl. 5.4: oxygen separated from fuel-gas cylinders by at least 20 ft (6.1 m) or a non-combustible barrier at least 5 ft (1.5 m) high, ½-hour fire resistance.

Question: According to the hose colour coding in KOC.SA.035 (BS EN ISO 3821), which colour hose is used for acetylene?
Reference: Cl. 5.7: Blue – Oxygen; Red – Acetylene; Orange – Propane, LPG, Natural Gas or Fuel Gas.

Question: Compressed gas cylinders must not be exposed to temperatures (including direct sunlight) exceeding:
Reference: Cl. 5.4: any cylinder containing compressed gas shall not be subjected to a temperature exceeding 54.5°C (130°F).

Question: Why must acetylene cylinders be stored, handled and used in the vertical position?
A: To let the porous mass settle evenly
B: To stop liquid acetone escaping to the valve
C: To keep the cylinder cooler in sunlight
D: To make the colour code easier to read
Reference: Cl. 5.1: acetylene is dissolved in acetone; cylinders must be kept vertical to prevent liquid acetone escaping and damaging valves and equipment.

Question: As a means of distinguishing gases, which valve outlet thread is used on acetylene, hydrogen and other flammable gas cylinders?
Reference: Cl. 5.2: right-hand thread for oxygen and non-flammable gases; left-hand thread for acetylene, hydrogen and flammable gases.

Question: A flashback occurs during oxy-acetylene cutting, but the hose looks intact from outside. What must be done with the hose?
A: Purge it with oxygen and continue the job
B: Leak test with soapy water and re-use if OK
C: Discard it immediately; the inner wall is damaged
D: Cut off the last metre and re-use the rest
Reference: Cl. 5.7: any hose in which a flashback has occurred will have its inner wall damaged and must be discarded immediately.

Question: After opening a gas cylinder valve fully for use, how should it be left?
A: Fully open against the back stop
B: A half turn back from full open
D: Fully open and taped in position
Reference: Cl. 5.5: an open valve shall be left a half turn back from full open so that movement to the back stop indicates the valve is open.

Question: 'Snifting' (briefly opening a cylinder valve to clear dirt before fitting a regulator) is permitted for most gases. For which gas is it NEVER allowed?
Reference: Cl. 5.5: hydrogen shall never be snifted as it may ignite spontaneously.

Question: What colour hose is used for oxygen under KOC.SA.035?
Reference: Cl. 5.7: Blue – Oxygen; Red – Acetylene; Orange – Propane / LPG / fuel gas.

Question: How must gas cylinder connections be checked for leaks?
A: A lighted match held near the joint
C: An oily cloth wiped over the joint
D: Soapy water or approved leak spray
Reference: Cl. 5.5: leak tests with mild soapy water or approved leak detection spray and NEVER by a naked flame.

Question: May a 12 kg domestic LPG cooking cylinder be used for pre-heating a pipeline?
A: Yes, with a fire extinguisher nearby
B: Yes, if a regulator is fitted
C: No, domestic cylinders are not allowed
Reference: Cl. 5.5: LPG cylinders intended for domestic purposes such as cooking shall not be used for welding, pre-heating or heating.

Question: Flammable substances shall not be stored within what distance of a gas cylinder storage area?
Reference: Cl. 5.4: flammable substances shall not be stored within 50 ft (15.25 m) of cylinder storage areas.

Question: If oxygen cylinders are stacked horizontally, what is the maximum number per tier?
Reference: Cl. 5.4: horizontal stacking in pyramid shape with not more than 15 numbers to a single tier; largest at the bottom.

Question: When cylinders are placed directly on forklift forks, how much of the fork length may they occupy?
Reference: Cl. 5.3: cylinders may be placed directly on the forks provided no more than 80% of the fork length is occupied.

Question: How should a gas cylinder be lifted by crane?
C: Slung with a chain round the body
D: Hooked by its valve or nozzle
Reference: Cl. 5.3: never lifted by valves, magnets or chains; strapped securely in a cradle.

Question: How should an oxy-acetylene torch be lit?
B: Acetylene first, with a friction lighter
C: Both gases together, with a cigarette lighter
Reference: Cl. 5.5 / 5.7: safe ignition with a friction lighter; torches are lit on acetylene first and oxygen used to adjust the flame.

Question: How far must an oxyacetylene blowpipe or other ignition source be kept from the oxygen and acetylene cylinders?
Reference: Cl. 5.5: blowpipe or approved ignition source kept at a distance of more than 5 m (16 ft) from acetylene and oxygen cylinders.

Question: What minimum maximum-dial reading must a contents gauge for an oxygen cylinder have?
Reference: Cl. 5.6: gauges for oxygen, nitrogen and hydrogen cylinders: max dial reading not less than 225 bar (acetylene: 40 bar).

Question: May full or empty oxygen and acetylene cylinders be transported alongside each other?
C: Yes, if valve caps are fitted
Reference: Cl. 5.3: oxygen and acetylene cylinders shall not be transported or stored alongside one another whether empty or full.

Question: How long must inspection records for cylinders, regulators, hoses and torches be retained?
Reference: Cl. 8.0: inspection records — six (6) months; test certificates — five years.

Question: According to KOC.HE.003, what is the permissible flammable gas limit for authorized cold work?
Reference: Cl. 5.6.1: the permissible limit for authorized cold work is below 10% of the LEL (hot work: 0% LEL).

Question: Where periodic gas testing is used during hot or cold work, the test interval must not exceed:
Reference: Cl. 5.6.1 / 5.6.3: testing continuously or periodically with the test interval not exceeding two hours.

Question: When gas testing for hot work, the gas test area shall include everywhere within what distance of the hot work location?
Reference: Cl. 5.7: the gas test area shall include everywhere within 50 ft (15 m) of the hot work location.

Question: A confined space is being mechanically ventilated by an exhaust fan. When should the gas test be carried out?
A: While the fan is running at full speed
B: Immediately after switching the fan off
C: About 10 minutes after stopping the exhaust fan
D: Only after the fan has been removed from the manway
Reference: Cl. 5.7: for a mechanically ventilated confined space, test only after 10 minutes of stopping the exhaust fan to avoid the effect of air draft.

Question: Which acceptable exposure levels (TLV-TWA) does KOC.HE.003 state for carbon monoxide and sulphur dioxide?
Reference: Cl. 5.3: acceptable levels — carbon monoxide 25 ppm (TLV-TWA, ACGIH) and sulphur dioxide 5 ppm (TLV-TWA, KEPA).

Question: Under the TLV-STEL definition in KOC.HE.003, exposures above the TLV-TWA up to the STEL should be:
A: Less than 15 minutes each, no more than 4 times a day, at least 60 minutes apart
B: Less than 30 minutes each, no more than 2 times a day, at least 30 minutes apart
C: Less than 15 minutes each, unlimited times a day
D: Less than 60 minutes each, once a day
Reference: Cl. 2.0: exposures above TWA up to STEL should be < 15 minutes, no more than four times per day, with at least 60 minutes between them.

Question: Which type of portable gas detector must be used for all INITIAL gas tests under KOC.HE.003?
B: Aspirated monitor with built-in sampling pump
C: Single-gas H2S badge clipped on the collar
D: Fixed area gas detector at the facility
Reference: Cl. 5.4.1: aspirated gas monitors (built-in pump) — all initial gas tests shall be done with this type of detector.

Question: When testing a vessel where H2S could be present, where is it essential to sample?
A: As close to the top of the vessel as possible
B: Only at the manway opening of the vessel
C: As close to the bottom of the vessel as possible
D: Only through the vessel's vent line
Reference: Cl. 5.5 / 5.7: H2S is heavier than air (1.19); sample as close to the bottom as possible.

Question: A gas detector is taken from an air-conditioned office to a hot outdoor worksite. What does KOC.HE.003 advise before using it?
A: Use it immediately, as sensors are temperature compensated
B: Allow 5–30 minutes for the instrument to stabilize to the temperature
C: Re-calibrate it in the field with test gas every time
D: Keep it in a plastic bag to avoid condensation during the test
Reference: Cl. 5.1: allow sufficient time for the equipment to temperature stabilize prior to use, which may vary between 5–30 minutes.

Question: What oxygen range does KOC.HE.003 state is required in the atmosphere tested?
Reference: Cl. 5.3: oxygen is normally 21%; required O2 is between 19.5% and 23.5%.

Question: Who carries out gas tests for work permits under KOC.HE.003?
Reference: Cl. 4.2 / 5.1: gas testing is carried out by Authorized Gas Testers, with results recorded on the permit.

Question: What is a 'bump test' of a gas detector?
A: A drop test to check the casing
B: A quick pre-use check with test gas
C: A check of battery charge level
Reference: Cl. 2.0: bump test — a quick functional test with a standard sample carried out prior to use (see KOC.GE.036).

Question: The calibration gas cylinder is past its expiry date. What does KOC.HE.003 say?
A: Never use test gas after its expiry
B: Use it while the cylinder is full
C: Use it if the readings look normal
D: Use it for bump tests only
Reference: Cl. 5.4.2: only use certified traceable test gas before its expiration date; never use a test gas after expiry.

Question: Who shall perform the calibration and certification of portable gas detectors (PGDs)?
B: Any trained operator on the site
D: The Permit Applicant for the job
Reference: Cl. 5.4.2: manufacturer or an accredited third party shall perform the calibration and certification of PGDs.

Question: Before using a portable gas detector, what must the user confirm on its calibration label?
A: Calibration expiry is after the issue date
B: The detector has been used at least once
C: Label colour matches the work area zone
D: The battery brand is on the approved list
Reference: Cl. 4.2 / 5.4: each PGD has a legible calibration label and the calibration expiry date is later than the issue date.

Question: When testing a confined space for a gas that is LIGHTER than air, such as acetylene, where should you test?
Reference: Cl. 5.7: test as low as possible for heavier gases and as high as possible for gases lighter than air (e.g. CO 0.97, acetylene 0.91).

Question: Where should the contents of a pipe be gas tested before it is broken into?
A: At the nearest storage tank vent outlet
B: Anywhere at all along the same line
C: As near the break-in point as possible
D: At the control room's fixed gas analyser
Reference: Cl. 5.5: test from a sampling point as near to the break-in point as possible, or on either side of it.

Question: A multi-gas detector is shared among several users. What should be done before each use?
A: Clean or disinfect it per the maker
D: Nothing, if the battery is charged
Reference: Cl. 5.1: a portable multi gas detector shared among multiple users should be disinfected / cleaned before use per manufacturer's recommendation.

Question: Who is the custodian of portable gas detectors, responsible for issuing them and ensuring timely maintenance and calibration?
Reference: Cl. 4.3: the Authorized Gas Tester is the custodian of all portable gas detectors, their issuance and timely maintenance and calibration.

Question: A tank atmosphere is above the Upper Explosive Limit (UEL). Why is this NOT a safe condition?
A: It is too lean to burn
B: Air ingress can make it flammable
C: It only affects toxic gas readings
D: It cannot be measured at all
Reference: Cl. 2.0: above UEL is 'too rich' to burn, but not a good basis for safety as added oxygen brings it into the flammable region.

Question: Who states on the Work Permit how long a gas test remains valid before a new test is required?
Reference: Cl. 4.3: the authorized gas tester states on the Work Permit how long the test is valid before a new gas test is required.

Question: Why should only manufacturer-approved sampling lines be used with a gas detector?
A: They may contain silicone that poisons sensors
B: Non-approved lines are too heavy to carry
C: Approved lines remove the need to calibrate
D: Approved lines are always much shorter
Reference: Cl. 5.1: a non-approved sampling line may contain silicone compounds which may poison the sensors.

Question: A contractor has 120 workers at a site. Under KOC.HE.004, what is the minimum number of first aiders required?
Reference: Cl. 5.4.1 c): one first aider per every 50 employees / contract workers (minimum one). 120 workers → 3 first aiders.

Question: What is the required provision of first aid kits under KOC.HE.004?
D: One kit per facility, regardless of numbers
Reference: Cl. 5.5 / 5.8: one first aid kit shall be made available for every 50 workers.

Question: To remain appropriately qualified, how often must a KOC first aider attend a first aid refresher course?
Reference: Cl. 5.5 B: first aiders attend refresher training courses every three (3) years.

Question: How often must designated first aiders attend a CPR and AED training session?
Reference: Cl. 5.5 B / 5.6.1: attend CPR & AED training session once every year.

Question: Under KOC.HE.004 and Kuwait labour requirements, a contractor must establish a First Aid Room wherever how many workers are engaged?
Reference: Cl. 5.4.1 a) / 5.5 II A: a First Aid Room shall be established wherever fifty (50) or more workers are engaged.

Question: Which statement about first aid kit containers is correct under KOC.HE.004?
A: Locked, to prevent theft of contents
B: Clearly labelled, visible and not locked
C: Opened only by the site medic
Reference: Cl. 5.8.1: the first aid container should be prominently displayed, labelled 'First Aid Box', accessible, and should not be locked.

Question: Within what time must a first aid case be reported in MyHSSE under KOC.HE.004 (with KOC.GE.007)?
Reference: Cl. 4: report in MyHSSE within 24 hours of incident occurrence (as per KOC.GE.007 & KOC.HE.020).

Question: Which statement best describes the role of a first aider under KOC.HE.004?
A: Give initial care within training; refer to medical advice
B: Provide ongoing treatment until full recovery
C: Prescribe medicines from the first aid kit stock
D: Decide whether the injury needs to be reported
Reference: Cl. 5.6: first aiders undertake initial treatment consistent with training; when in doubt recommend medical advice; not responsible for ongoing care.

Question: What minimum first aid cover must Team Leaders ensure in each work area or operating facility?
A: One first aider per facility for all shifts
B: One first aider per day shift only
C: At least one first aider per shift
D: A first aider only when 50 workers are present
Reference: Cl. 4.6: ensure at least one first aider per shift in each work area / operation facility.

Question: How often must a First Aid Needs Assessment be reviewed, unless changes occur earlier?
Reference: Cl. 5.3: assessments made initially and reviewed once in three years, or earlier if layout, staff numbers or hazards change.

Question: What does an Automated External Defibrillator (AED) do?
Reference: Cl. 2.2: AED analyzes the heartbeat, advises action and delivers a calibrated electric shock.

Question: Which qualification meets KOC.HE.004 requirements for a Contractor Medic?
A: Driving licence and a basic first aid course
B: EMT diploma or B.Sc. Nursing, BLS/AED, 2 yrs
C: Safety officer certificate and 1 year's service
D: Any first aid certificate, 6 months' service
Reference: Cl. 2.5: 2-yr EMT diploma or B.Sc (Nursing); AHA BLS with AED current certification; minimum 2 years' experience.

Question: Which first aid treatments must be recorded in the First Aid Register?
Reference: Cl. 4.11: first aiders record all treatment (however minor) on the First Aid Register.

Question: A first aider learns medical information about a casualty. Who may it be released to?
Reference: Cl. 4.11: keep confidential all information; medical information must only be released to relevant medical staff.

Question: How long is the 'Train-the-Trainers' first aid programme organized by the HSE Induction Center?
Reference: Cl. 5.6.1: HSE Induction Center shall organize a 3-day 'Train-the-Trainers' programme.

Question: Workers who handled paint or chemicals must do what before taking meals?
Reference: Cl. 5.1: persons handling chemicals, paint or toxic substances must thoroughly wash their hands before meals and before leaving site.

Question: What must be done with an eye wash bottle once it has been opened?
A: Close it and keep it for next use
B: Keep it in the kit for one month
D: Dispose of it and replace it
Reference: Cl. 5.12: eye wash bottles once opened should be disposed of and replenished.

Question: Who initiates the First Aid Needs Assessment?
Reference: Cl. 4.6 / 5.3: the concerned Group HSE Officer / HSE Coordinator / nominee shall initiate the First Aid Need Assessment.

Question: Cardio Pulmonary Resuscitation (CPR) combines which two actions?
D: Cooling the body and giving oral fluids
Reference: Cl. 2.4: CPR combines rescue breathing and chest compressions.

Question: Where is a Contractor Medic required to staff a First Aid Room?
A: At rig camps and remote locations
Reference: Cl. 5.5 II E: Contractor Medic is required in First Aid Rooms at rig camps and remote locations.

Question: In an open yard storage area, what is the maximum height to which combustible materials may be piled?
Reference: Cl. 5.2.1: combustible materials shall in no case be piled higher than 20 ft (6.1 m).

Question: What minimum width must driveways between and around combustible storage piles be kept?
Reference: Cl. 5.2.1: driveways between and around combustible storage piles must be at least 15 ft (4.57 m) wide.

Question: Under KOC.GE.034, combustible material may NOT be stored outdoors within what distance of a building or structure?
Reference: Cl. 5.2.1: no combustible material may be stored outdoors within 10 ft (3.048 m) of a building or structure.

Question: In an indoor store with sprinklers, what minimum clearance must be kept between the top of stored material and the sprinkler deflectors?
Reference: Cl. 5.2.2: clearance of at least 36 inches (0.9144 m) must be maintained between stored material and sprinkler deflectors.

Question: Non-compatible materials that may create a fire, explosion or reaction hazard must be segregated in storage by a barrier with a fire resistance of at least:
Reference: Cl. 5.2.2: non-compatible materials must be segregated by a barrier having a fire resistance of at least 1 hour.

Question: Where needed for access to doors, windows or standpipe connections, aisles must be kept at least how wide?
Reference: Cl. 5.3: keep aisles at least 3 ft (0.9144 m) wide where necessary for access to doors, windows or standpipe connections.

Question: What does KOC.GE.034 recommend regarding end-of-day cleaning on construction sites?
A: Cleaning is done by a separate night crew only
B: Work stops half an hour early for site cleaning
C: Housekeeping is done once a week on rest day
D: Cleaning is needed only before HSE inspections
Reference: Cl. 5.0 Note: it is highly recommended that construction activities cease half an hour before and that time be used for area cleaning / housekeeping.

Question: Under KOC.GE.034, what must Team Leaders ensure regarding gasoline within the battery limits of KOC projects, facilities and drilling sites?
A: Gasoline may be stored in approved jerry cans up to 20 litres
B: No gasoline storage or refuelling is allowed
C: Gasoline may be stored if kept 15 m from buildings
D: Gasoline refuelling is allowed only during daylight
Reference: Cl. 4.1: ensure that no gasoline storage or its refuelling is allowed in the KOC jurisdiction battery limit of any projects / facilities / drilling sites.

Question: Which phrase sums up housekeeping in KOC.GE.034?
A: A place for everything, everything in its place
B: Clean up only before HSE inspections
C: Store all materials close to the work face
D: Remove site waste once a month
Reference: Cl. 1.0 / 5.2: 'Housekeeping is about a place for everything and everything in its place'.

Question: When must crude oil, chemical or diesel spills be cleaned up?
B: At the end of the shift
Reference: Cl. 5.1: crude oil / chemical / diesel spills shall be cleaned immediately; contaminated soil disposed per KOC.EV.007 / EV.008.

Question: May electrical rooms or computer server rooms be used to store materials?
A: Yes, if proper shelves are fitted
C: Yes, but only for spare parts
D: No, not for materials of any kind
Reference: Cl. 5.2.2: electric rooms and computer server rooms are not to be used as storage rooms for materials of any kind.

Question: What minimum distance must stored material be kept from a fire door opening?
Reference: Cl. 5.2.2: material must not be stored within 36 inches (0.9144 m) of a fire door opening.

Question: Lumber that will be handled manually shall not be stacked higher than:
Reference: Cl. 5.2.2: lumber piles shall not exceed 20 ft; lumber handled manually shall not be stacked more than 16 ft (4.876 m).

Question: What clearance must be kept around the path of travel of a fire door, unless a barricade is provided?
Reference: Cl. 5.2.2: a clearance of 24 inches must be maintained around the path of travel of fire doors unless a barricade is provided.

Question: How should protruding reinforcement bars (rebars) on site be protected?
A: Left as they are, with a sign
Reference: Cl. 5.1: protruding rebars are to be provided with rebar caps to avoid personal injury.

Question: Where must food and beverages NOT be stored?
Reference: Cl. 5.1: no food or beverages shall be stored in toilet rooms or in an area exposed to toxic materials.

Question: Driveways between combustible storage piles must be spaced to give a maximum grid unit of:
Reference: Cl. 5.2.1: driveways must be so spaced that a maximum grid system unit of 50 ft by 150 ft is produced.

Question: Who is responsible for good housekeeping in their own work area?
Reference: Cl. 4.3 / 5.0: employees are responsible for good housekeeping in their respective work areas; housekeeping is everyone's responsibility.

Question: Inside a building under construction, material shall not be placed within what distance of a hoistway or floor opening?
Reference: Cl. 5.2.2: material shall not be placed within 6 feet of any hoistway or inside floor openings.

Question: After a dust storm, how should dusty floors inside buildings be cleaned?
A: Wait for the next weekly cleaning
B: Blow it away with compressed air
C: Hose it down with plenty of water
Reference: Cl. 5.5: dusty floors cleaned as soon as possible after dust storms; vacuuming or soft-bristle sweeping to minimize airborne dust.

Question: A worker's personal H2S monitor goes into alarm near a sour wellhead. What is the correct immediate response under KOC.GE.036?
A: Run downwind to the nearest vehicle and drive off
B: Don escape set, check windsock, walk crosswind
C: Stay in place and wait for Control Room instructions
D: Help colleagues nearer the release before leaving
Reference: Cl. 5.x Escape from H2S Release: put on escape-only respirator, observe windsock, walk (don't run) crosswind to Control Room / muster point; do not attempt to rescue others.

Question: When purchasing personal H2S monitors, KOC.GE.036 recommends two alarm set points. What are they?
A: First alarm at or below 5 ppm; second at or below 10 ppm
B: First alarm at or below 10 ppm; second at or below 15 ppm
C: First alarm at or below 15 ppm; second at or below 50 ppm
D: First alarm at or below 20 ppm; second at or below 100 ppm
Reference: Cl. 5.3 c): units should alarm at or below 10 ppm (TWA/8 hrs) for the first alarm and at or below 15 ppm (STEL/15 min) for the second.

Question: According to KOC.GE.036 Table 2, when H2S is between 10 and 15 ppm, work without respiratory protection is permitted for:
B: 15 min, up to 4 times per shift
C: 30 min, up to 2 times per shift
Reference: Table 2: between 10 to 15 ppm, work is permitted for a 15-minute period without RPE, up to 4 times during an 8-hour shift.

Question: Gas testing shows 60 ppm H2S at a worksite and the source cannot be isolated, purged or ventilated. Under KOC.GE.036, what is required for work to proceed?
D: No work is allowed above 50 ppm
Reference: Table 2: up to 100 ppm, work is permitted with positive-pressure supplied air respirator or 30-min SCBA only if the source cannot be isolated; above 100 ppm entry only for rescue.

Question: Where should a personal H2S monitor be worn?
A: Inside the coverall pocket, away from dust
B: On the belt at waist level
Reference: Cl. 5.3 c): worn outside clothing close to the head, as this is where H2S will be ingested; shoulder or breast pocket is optimal.

Question: A crew of 14 workers will carry out maintenance in an area where H2S hazards may be present, but the facility itself is not sour. What gas detection does KOC.GE.036 require?
A: One personal gas monitor for the crew
C: No detector, as the facility is not sour
D: One personal monitor per five workers
Reference: Cl. 4 Field Workers c): one personal monitor per crew below 10 workers; more than 10 workers — a tripod-mounted portable multi-gas detector; sour facility — every worker carries one.

Question: KOC.GE.036 defines 'sour' hydrocarbons as oil or gas containing H2S above:
Reference: Cl. 2.0: sour hydrocarbons contain more than 0.001%, i.e. 10 ppm of hydrogen sulphide.

Question: Why can opening a vessel that handled sour product be hazardous even after it has been drained?
A: Dry pyrophoric iron sulphide can self-ignite in air
B: H2S turns lighter than air once the vessel is open
C: Rust deposits stop portable gas detectors working
D: Sulphur dioxide is released when water is added
Reference: Cl. 5.2 f): pyrophoric scale (ferrous sulphide) reacts exothermically with oxygen and, when dry, auto-ignites at ambient temperature.

Question: How often must personnel who may enter H2S hazardous areas receive H2S awareness training under KOC.GE.036?
Reference: Cl. 5.4 a): personnel who may be required to enter H2S hazardous areas shall receive annual H2S awareness.

Question: Which description of hydrogen sulphide (H2S) is correct?
A: Colourless, heavier than air, rotten-egg smell
B: Colourless, lighter than air, garlic smell
C: Brown, heavier than air, no smell at all
D: Yellow, lighter than air, no smell at all
Reference: Cl. 2.0: H2S is a colourless, very toxic, corrosive, heavier than air, flammable gas with a strong odour of rotten eggs.

Question: Why must workers NOT rely on smell to detect H2S?
A: Its smell can only be noticed indoors
B: It smells exactly the same as diesel
C: It has no smell at any concentration
D: It deadens the sense of smell quickly
Reference: Table 2 (IDLH): H2S deadens sense of smell in 3 to 15 minutes.

Question: How must the facility sour gas alarm signal differ from the normal siren?
C: The same tone as the fire alarm
D: A silent signal, using lights only
Reference: Cl. 5.3 b): the sour gas alarm signal shall be different from the normal siren and easily recognisable.

Question: Work is planned 700 m from a sour gas facility. What does KOC.GE.036 require regarding windsocks?
A: Windsocks only if work exceeds 8 hours a day
C: None, as the work is outside the facility fence
D: A single windsock at the facility's main gate
Reference: Cl. 5.4 c): all facilities and work within 1 km of sour gas facilities shall have windsocks indicating which way to escape.

Question: How many escape routes and assembly points should the JSA consider for work in an H2S area?
C: At least two routes, one assembly point
D: One route, at least two assembly points
Reference: Cl. 5.4 d): escape routes (at least two) and assembly points (at least two), depending on the location of the potential incident.

Question: A colleague collapses near a sour wellhead. Under KOC.GE.036, what must you NOT do?
C: Move crosswind to the muster point
Reference: Cl. 4.9 h) / 5.5 c): workers shall not attempt rescue without SCBA; personnel shall not rescue others without first protecting themselves.

Question: What respiratory protection must a trained rescuer wear when attempting rescue in an H2S release?
Reference: Cl. 5.5 c): positive-pressure, 30-minute SCBA shall always be worn when attempting rescue, with a standby person.

Question: An H2S-exposed worker has red, painful eyes. How long should the eyes be flushed with clean water?
Reference: Cl. 5.5 d): if the victim's eyes are red and painful, flush with large amounts of clean water for at least 15 minutes.

Question: Under the Ministry of Oil Regulations quoted in KOC.GE.036, how must work in a sour crude or sour gas environment be staffed?
A: With a supervisor visiting every hour
B: Alone, if he is carrying a radio
C: Alone, if wearing a personal H2S monitor
Reference: Cl. 3.1: no person shall work in a sour crude oil or sour gas environment without the continuous attendance of another person.

Question: What minimum measuring range must a personal H2S monitor have?
Reference: Cl. 5.3 c): the measuring range shall cover at least 0 to 100 ppm with continuous read-out.

Question: How often must the Asset / Directorate HSE Team carry out the H2S Hazard Management inspection of detection systems and RPE?
Reference: Cl. 4.7 d): carry out biannual 'HSE Inspection' using the H2S Hazard Management Inspection Checklist (Appendix 6).

Question: Where must muster points be available around a work location in an H2S area?
A: Only at the main facility gate
C: On both sides (90°) of the work
D: Only downwind of the work area
Reference: Cl. 4.5 g): ensure that muster points are available on both sides (90 degree) of the work location.

Question: The permanent place of safety in a Sour Gas Release Contingency Plan must always remain below what H2S level?
Reference: Cl. 5.5 a) x: a permanent place of safety shall always remain below 10 ppm (8 Hour TWA).

Question: What is the minimum isolation standard required for entry into a vessel or confined space under KOC.PS.016?
A: Single block valve, locked and tagged
B: Double block and bleed valve isolation
D: ESD valve closed with actuator enabled
Reference: Cl. 5.1 / 5.5.1: the minimum isolation standard for vessel or confined space entry is positive isolation; it is mandatory for such entry.

Question: Which is the PREFERRED method of achieving positive isolation according to KOC.PS.016?
A: Closing two block valves with an open bleed
B: Spool removal with rated blank flanges on the live ends
C: Inserting a spade only when spool removal is easier
D: Closing a single gate valve and locking it
Reference: Cl. 5.5.1: spool removal is the preferred method of positive isolation; spade insertion where spool removal is not reasonably practicable; valves alone are not positive isolation.

Question: Before breaking containment, how long does KOC.PS.016 recommend that isolation integrity tests be conducted, as a minimum?
Reference: Cl. 5.7: all isolations shall be tested and shown to be effective before containment is broken; integrity tests recommended for a minimum of 10 minutes.

Question: What is the minimum recommended frequency for monitoring the integrity of isolation points while containment is broken?
A: Once per week, at the start of the work week
B: Once per day, at the start of day shift only
C: Once per shift and just before breaking containment
D: Only when the Work Party requests a check
Reference: Cl. 5.8: minimum recommended monitoring frequency is once per shift and immediately prior to breaking containment; results recorded at shift handover.

Question: Which type of valve shall NOT be used as a form of isolation under KOC.PS.016?
D: Fail-closed ESD valve with actuator disabled
Reference: Cl. 5.9: non-return (check) valves, flow control valves and pressure relief valves shall not be used as a form of isolation.

Question: During work under a double block and bleed isolation, the gauge on the bleed between the two block valves starts to show pressure. What must happen?
A: Open the bleed fully and continue working
B: Stop work and review and amend the isolation
C: Tighten the upstream valve and continue
D: Record it at shift handover and continue
Reference: Cl. 5.5.2: the void between block valves must remain at 0 barg; if pressure increases, work shall stop and the isolation be reviewed and amended.

Question: Besides vessel entry, KOC.PS.016 recommends positive isolation for long-duration isolations. What duration is given as an example?
Reference: Cl. 5.5.1: positive isolation recommended for long duration isolations, e.g. more than one week, hot work, and new/out-of-service equipment interfaces.

Question: Under KOC.PS.016, how are bleeds and vents that form part of an isolation to be controlled?
A: Padlocked shut like the block valves
B: Left untagged so they can be operated
C: Tagged and recorded, without a lock
D: Removed from the line and blanked
Reference: Cl. 5.13: bleeds and vents do not require a securing device, as their position may change, but they require a bleed/vent tag and must be documented on the Certificate.

Question: Which of the following is a form of positive isolation?
B: A closed and locked gate valve
Reference: Cl. 2.0 / 5.5.1: positive isolation is physical separation, e.g. blinding, spading, spool removal or air gapping.

Question: Why is valve isolation alone NOT regarded as positive isolation?
D: Valves are too slow to close
Reference: Cl. 5.5.1: valve isolation alone is not sufficient to be classified as positive isolation because of the potential for valves to leak.

Question: Who prepares the Mechanical Isolation Certificate?
Reference: Cl. 4.3 / 5.4: the Authorised Isolator plans and prepares the isolation by completing the Mechanical Isolation Certificate.

Question: Who is ultimately responsible for ensuring the installed isolation is correct and authorizing the isolation work to proceed?
Reference: Cl. 4.2: the PRA is ultimately responsible for ensuring the isolation is correct and for authorizing the isolation work.

Question: What right does the Work Party (Performing Authority) have regarding an isolation?
A: To remove locks during break time
B: To ask for proof of isolation integrity
Reference: Cl. 4.4: the Performing Authority has the right to request demonstration of the integrity of any isolation.

Question: When may pressure, vacuum or thermal relief valves be isolated during an isolation?
A: Only after full isolation with vents open
C: First, before any other valve is closed
D: Whenever the Work Party requests it
Reference: Cl. 5.4 Note 3: do not isolate relief valves until the equipment is fully isolated and adequate vents are open.

Question: An electrically operated valve is used as an isolation point. What is required?
A: A tag on the valve only
C: Nothing extra if it is closed
Reference: Cl. 5.6.2: electrically operated valves shall have their power supply positively isolated and locked.

Question: Pneumatically operated valves that FAIL OPEN should normally:
C: Be used with air supply connected
Reference: Cl. 5.6.2: pneumatically and hydraulically operated valves which fail open should not normally be used for isolation purposes.

Question: What material must isolation tags be made of?
Reference: Cl. 5.14: all tags must be made of plastic or other weatherproofing material and secured against accidental removal.

Question: An isolation valve cannot be locked and could be opened by accidental contact. What should be done?
A: Paint the valve handle bright red
C: Tie the handle with plastic tape
D: Leave it and fit a second tag
Reference: Cl. 5.6.2: when isolating any valve that cannot be locked, the valve handle shall be removed where practicable.

Question: Under what condition may an ESD valve be used for isolation?
A: Fail-open, with air supply left on
D: Used only as a bleed valve
Reference: Cl. 5.9: ESD valves may be used for isolation provided they are fail closed and the actuator is disabled.

Question: An isolation valve is found to be passing slightly. What must be done before deciding whether work can proceed?
A: Tell HSE Group after the job
D: Proceed, as the leak is small
Reference: Cl. 5.9.1: whenever an isolation is compromised by passing valves, a risk assessment must be made of each isolation point.
